fields.name: client_protocol
fields.note: ClientProtocol is the protocol version of the player. The player is disconnected if the protocol is incompatible with the protocol of the server. It has been superseded by the protocol version sent in the RequestNetworkSettings packet, so this should no longer be used by the server.

fields.name: connection_request
fields.note: ConnectionRequest is a string containing information about the player and JWTs that may be used to verify if the player is connected to XBOX Live. The connection request also contains the necessary client public key to initiate encryption.

fields.name: reason
fields.note: Reason is the reason for the disconnection. It seems as if this field has no use other than for telemetry reasons as it does not affect the message that gets displayed on the disconnect screen.

fields.name: hide_disconnection_screen
fields.note: HideDisconnectionScreen specifies if the disconnection screen should be hidden when the client is disconnected, meaning it will be sent directly to the main menu.

fields.name: message
fields.note: Message is an optional message to show when disconnected. This message is only written if the HideDisconnectionScreen field is set to true.

fields.name: filtered_message
fields.note: FilteredMessage is a filtered version of Message with all the profanity removed. The client will use this over Message if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

fields.name: texture_pack_required
fields.note: TexturePackRequired specifies if the client must accept the texture packs the server has in order to join the server. If set to true, the client gets the option to either download the resource packs and join, or quit entirely. Behaviour packs never have to be downloaded.

fields.name: has_addons
fields.note: HasAddons specifies if any of the resource packs contain addons in them. If set to true, only clients that support addons will be able to download them.

fields.name: has_scripts
fields.note: HasScripts specifies if any of the resource packs contain scripts in them. If set to true, only clients that support scripts will be able to download them.

fields.name: force_disable_vibrant_visuals
fields.note: ForceDisableVibrantVisuals specifies if the vibrant visuals feature should be forcibly disabled on the server. If set to true, the server will ensure that vibrant visuals are not enabled, regardless of the client's settings.

fields.name: world_template_uuid
fields.note: WorldTemplateUUID is the UUID of the template that has been used to generate the world. Templates can be downloaded from the marketplace or installed via '.mctemplate' files. If the world was not generated from a template, this field is empty.

fields.name: world_template_version
fields.note: WorldTemplateVersion is the version of the world template that has been used to generate the world. If the world was not generated from a template, this field is empty.

fields.name: texture_packs
fields.note: TexturePacks is a list of texture packs that the client needs to download before joining the server. The order of these texture packs is not relevant in this packet. It is however important in the ResourcePackStack packet.

children.name: uuid
children.note: UUID is the UUID of the texture pack. Each texture pack downloaded must have a different UUID in order for the client to be able to handle them properly.

children.name: version
children.note: Version is the version of the texture pack. The client will cache texture packs sent by the server as long as they carry the same version. Sending a texture pack with a different version than previously will force the client to re-download it.

children.name: size
children.note: Size is the total size in bytes that the texture pack occupies. This is the size of the compressed archive (zip) of the texture pack.

children.name: content_key
children.note: ContentKey is the key used to decrypt the behaviour pack if it is encrypted. This is generally the case for marketplace texture packs.

children.name: sub_pack_name
children.note: SubPackName ...

children.name: content_identity
children.note: ContentIdentity is another UUID for the resource pack, and is generally set for marketplace texture packs. It is also required for client-side validations when the resource pack is encrypted.

children.name: has_scripts
children.note: HasScripts specifies if the texture packs has any scripts in it. A client will only download the behaviour pack if it supports scripts, which, up to 1.11, only includes Windows 10.

children.name: addon_pack
children.note: AddonPack specifies if the texture pack is from an addon.

children.name: rtxenabled
children.note: RTXEnabled specifies if the texture pack uses the raytracing technology introduced in 1.16.200.

children.name: download_url
children.note: DownloadURL is a URL that the client can use to download the pack instead of the server sending it in chunks, which it will continue to do if this field is left empty.

packets.name: ResourcePacksInfo
packets.title: 资源包信息
packets.usage: 服务器提供资源包列表；可检查服务器要求加载的资源包。
packets.description: ResourcePacksInfo is sent by the server to inform the client on what resource packs the server has. It sends a list of the resource packs it has and basic information on them like the version and description.
packets.content:
## 6 · ResourcePacksInfo · 资源包信息

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：服务器提供资源包列表；可检查服务器要求加载的资源包。
- 本内核原始说明：ResourcePacksInfo is sent by the server to inform the client on what resource packs the server has. It sends a list of the resource packs it has and basic information on them like the version and description.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `texture_pack_required` | `bool` | TexturePackRequired specifies if the client must accept the texture packs the server has in order to join the server. If set to true, the client gets the option to either download the resource packs and join, or quit entirely. Behaviour packs never have to be downloaded. |
| `has_addons` | `bool` | HasAddons specifies if any of the resource packs contain addons in them. If set to true, only clients that support addons will be able to download them. |
| `has_scripts` | `bool` | HasScripts specifies if any of the resource packs contain scripts in them. If set to true, only clients that support scripts will be able to download them. |
| `force_disable_vibrant_visuals` | `bool` | ForceDisableVibrantVisuals specifies if the vibrant visuals feature should be forcibly disabled on the server. If set to true, the server will ensure that vibrant visuals are not enabled, regardless of the client's settings. |
| `world_template_uuid` | `uuid.UUID` | WorldTemplateUUID is the UUID of the template that has been used to generate the world. Templates can be downloaded from the marketplace or installed via '.mctemplate' files. If the world was not generated from a template, this field is empty. |
| `world_template_version` | `string` | WorldTemplateVersion is the version of the world template that has been used to generate the world. If the world was not generated from a template, this field is empty. |
| `texture_packs` | `[]protocol.TexturePackInfo` | TexturePacks is a list of texture packs that the client needs to download before joining the server. The order of these texture packs is not relevant in this packet. It is however important in the ResourcePackStack packet. |

### texture_packs 嵌套字段

- `uuid` (`uuid.UUID`)：UUID is the UUID of the texture pack. Each texture pack downloaded must have a different UUID in order for the client to be able to handle them properly.
- `version` (`string`)：Version is the version of the texture pack. The client will cache texture packs sent by the server as long as they carry the same version. Sending a texture pack with a different version than previously will force the client to re-download it.
- `size` (`uint64`)：Size is the total size in bytes that the texture pack occupies. This is the size of the compressed archive (zip) of the texture pack.
- `content_key` (`string`)：ContentKey is the key used to decrypt the behaviour pack if it is encrypted. This is generally the case for marketplace texture packs.
- `sub_pack_name` (`string`)：SubPackName ...
- `content_identity` (`string`)：ContentIdentity is another UUID for the resource pack, and is generally set for marketplace texture packs. It is also required for client-side validations when the resource pack is encrypted.
- `has_scripts` (`bool`)：HasScripts specifies if the texture packs has any scripts in it. A client will only download the behaviour pack if it supports scripts, which, up to 1.11, only includes Windows 10.
- `addon_pack` (`bool`)：AddonPack specifies if the texture pack is from an addon.
- `rtxenabled` (`bool`)：RTXEnabled specifies if the texture pack uses the raytracing technology introduced in 1.16.200.
- `download_url` (`string`)：DownloadURL is a URL that the client can use to download the pack instead of the server sending it in chunks, which it will continue to do if this field is left empty.

packets.name: ResourcePackStack
packets.title: 资源包栈
packets.usage: 用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
packets.description: ResourcePackStack is sent by the server to send the order in which resource packs and behaviour packs should be applied (and downloaded) by the client.
packets.content:
## 7 · ResourcePackStack · 资源包栈

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
- 本内核原始说明：ResourcePackStack is sent by the server to send the order in which resource packs and behaviour packs should be applied (and downloaded) by the client.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `texture_pack_required` | `bool` | TexturePackRequired specifies if the client must accept the texture packs the server has in order to join the server. If set to true, the client gets the option to either download the resource packs and join, or quit entirely. Behaviour packs never have to be downloaded. |
| `behaviour_packs` | `[]protocol.StackResourcePack` | BehaviourPack is a list of behaviour packs that the client needs to download before joining the server. All of these behaviour packs will be applied together, and the order does not necessarily matter. |
| `texture_packs` | `[]protocol.StackResourcePack` | TexturePacks is a list of texture packs that the client needs to download before joining the server. The order of these texture packs specifies the order that they are applied in on the client side. The first in the list will be applied first. |
| `base_game_version` | `string` | BaseGameVersion is the vanilla version that the client should set its resource pack stack to. |
| `experiments` | `[]protocol.ExperimentData` | Experiments holds a list of experiments that are either enabled or disabled in the world that the player spawns in. It is not clear why experiments are sent both here and in the StartGame packet. |
| `experiments_previously_toggled` | `bool` | ExperimentsPreviouslyToggled specifies if any experiments were previously toggled in this world. It is probably used for some kind of metrics. |
| `include_editor_packs` | `bool` | IncludeEditorPacks specifies if vanilla editor packs should be included in the resource pack stack when connecting to an editor world. |

### behaviour_packs 嵌套字段

- `uuid` (`string`)：UUID is the UUID of the resource pack. Each resource pack downloaded must have a different UUID in order for the client to be able to handle them properly.
- `version` (`string`)：Version is the version of the resource pack. The client will cache resource packs sent by the server as long as they carry the same version. Sending a resource pack with a different version than previously will force the client to re-download it.
- `sub_pack_name` (`string`)：SubPackName ...

### texture_packs 嵌套字段

- `uuid` (`string`)：UUID is the UUID of the resource pack. Each resource pack downloaded must have a different UUID in order for the client to be able to handle them properly.
- `version` (`string`)：Version is the version of the resource pack. The client will cache resource packs sent by the server as long as they carry the same version. Sending a resource pack with a different version than previously will force the client to re-download it.
- `sub_pack_name` (`string`)：SubPackName ...

### experiments 嵌套字段

- `name` (`string`)：Name is the name of the experiment.
- `enabled` (`bool`)：Enabled specifies if the experiment is enabled. Vanilla typically always sets this to true for any experiments sent.

fields.name: text_type
fields.note: TextType is the type of the text sent. When a client sends this to the server, it should always be TextTypeChat. If the server sends it, it may be one of the other text types above.

fields.name: needs_translation
fields.note: NeedsTranslation specifies if any of the messages need to be translated. It seems that where % is found in translatable text types, these are translated regardless of this bool. Translatable text types include TextTypeTranslation, TextTypeTip, TextTypePopup and TextTypeJukeboxPopup.

fields.name: source_name
fields.note: SourceName is the name of the source of the messages. This source is displayed in text types such as the TextTypeChat and TextTypeWhisper, where typically the username is shown.

fields.name: message
fields.note: Message is the message of the packet. This field is set for each TextType and is the main component of the packet.

fields.name: parameters
fields.note: Parameters is a list of parameters that should be filled into the message. These parameters are only written if the type of the packet is TextTypeTranslation, TextTypeTip, TextTypePopup or TextTypeJukeboxPopup.

fields.name: xuid
fields.note: XUID is the XBOX Live user ID of the player that sent the message. It is only set for packets of TextTypeChat. When sent to a player, the player will only be shown the chat message if a player with this XUID is present in the player list and not muted, or if the XUID is empty.

fields.name: platform_chat_id
fields.note: PlatformChatID is an identifier only set for particular platforms when chatting (presumably only for Nintendo Switch). It is otherwise an empty string, and is used to decide which players are able to chat with each other.

fields.name: filtered_message
fields.note: FilteredMessage is a filtered version of Message with all the profanity removed. The client will use this over Message if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

fields.name: unknown1
fields.note: PhoenixBuilder specific fields. Author: Liliya233, Happy2018new  The following fields are NetEase specific.

It seems that where % is found in translatable text types, these are translated regardless of this bool. Translatable text types include TextTypeTranslation, TextTypeTip, TextTypePopup and TextTypeJukeboxPopup. |

| `parameters` | `[]string` | Parameters is a list of parameters that should be filled into the message. These parameters are only written if the type of the packet is TextTypeTranslation, TextTypeTip, TextTypePopup or TextTypeJukeboxPopup. |

packets.name: SetTime
packets.title: 世界时间同步
packets.usage: 仅按服务器真实Time观测游戏时间和TPS；玩家手动/time会改时间，不用现实时间硬算永久昼夜。
packets.description: SetTime is sent by the server to update the current time client-side. The client actually advances time client-side by itself, so this packet does not need to be sent each tick. It is merely a means of synchronising time between server and client.
packets.content:
## 10 · SetTime · 世界时间同步

- 分组：世界与结构
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：仅按服务器真实Time观测游戏时间和TPS；玩家手动/time会改时间，不用现实时间硬算永久昼夜。
- 本内核原始说明：SetTime is sent by the server to update the current time client-side. The client actually advances time client-side by itself, so this packet does not need to be sent each tick. It is merely a means of synchronising time between server and client.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `time` | `int32` | Time is the current time. The time is not limited to 24000 (time of day), but continues progressing after that. |

fields.name: entity_unique_id
fields.note: 实体唯一ID，与运行ID不同。 EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the player. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for this field.

fields.name: entity_runtime_id
fields.note: 当前会话实体运行ID，不同会话不能复用；64位ID建议传十进制字符串。 EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: player_game_mode
fields.note: PlayerGameMode is the game mode the player currently has. It is a value from 0-4, with 0 being survival mode, 1 being creative mode, 2 being adventure mode, 3 being survival spectator and 4 being creative spectator. This field may be set to 5 to make the client fall back to the game mode set in the WorldGameMode field.

fields.name: player_position
fields.note: PlayerPosition is the spawn position of the player in the world. In servers this is often the same as the world's spawn position found below.

fields.name: pitch
fields.note: 俯仰角。 Pitch is the vertical rotation of the player. Facing straight forward yields a pitch of 0. Pitch is measured in degrees.

fields.name: yaw
fields.note: 偏航角。 Yaw is the horizontal rotation of the player. Yaw is also measured in degrees.

fields.name: world_seed
fields.note: WorldSeed is the seed used to generate the world. Unlike in PC edition, the seed is a 32bit integer here.

fields.name: spawn_biome_type
fields.note: SpawnBiomeType specifies if the biome that the player spawns in is user defined (through behaviour packs) or builtin. See the constants above.

fields.name: user_defined_biome_name
fields.note: UserDefinedBiomeName is a readable name of the biome that the player spawned in, such as 'plains'. This might be a custom biome name if any custom biomes are present through behaviour packs.

fields.name: dimension
fields.note: Dimension is the ID of the dimension that the player spawns in. It is a value from 0-2, with 0 being the overworld, 1 being the nether and 2 being the end.

fields.name: generator
fields.note: Generator is the generator used for the world. It is a value from 0-4, with 0 being old limited worlds, 1 being infinite worlds, 2 being flat worlds, 3 being nether worlds and 4 being end worlds. A value of 0 will actually make the client stop rendering chunks you send beyond the world limit.

fields.name: world_game_mode
fields.note: WorldGameMode is the game mode that a player gets when it first spawns in the world. It is shown in the settings and is used if the PlayerGameMode is set to 5.

fields.name: hardcore
fields.note: Hardcore is if the world is in hardcore mode. In hardcore mode, the player cannot respawn after dying.

fields.name: difficulty
fields.note: Difficulty is the difficulty of the world. It is a value from 0-3, with 0 being peaceful, 1 being easy, 2 being normal and 3 being hard.

fields.name: world_spawn
fields.note: WorldSpawn is the block on which the world spawn of the world. This coordinate has no effect on the place that the client spawns, but it does have an effect on the direction that a compass points.

fields.name: achievements_disabled
fields.note: AchievementsDisabled defines if achievements are disabled in the world. The client crashes if this value is set to true while the player's or the world's game mode is creative, and it's recommended to simply always set this to false as a server.

fields.name: editor_world_type
fields.note: EditorWorldType is a value to dictate the type of editor mode, a special mode recently introduced adding "powerful tools for editing worlds, intended for experienced creators." It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: created_in_editor
fields.note: CreatedInEditor is a value to dictate if the world was created as a project in the editor mode. The functionality of this field is currently unknown.

fields.name: exported_from_editor
fields.note: ExportedFromEditor is a value to dictate if the world was exported from editor mode. The functionality of this field is currently unknown.

fields.name: day_cycle_lock_time
fields.note: DayCycleLockTime is the time at which the day cycle was locked if the day cycle is disabled using the respective game rule. The client will maintain this time as long as the day cycle is disabled.

fields.name: education_edition_offer
fields.note: EducationEditionOffer is some Minecraft: Education Edition field that specifies what 'region' the world was from, with 0 being None, 1 being RestOfWorld, and 2 being China. The actual use of this field is unknown.

fields.name: education_features_enabled
fields.note: EducationFeaturesEnabled specifies if the world has education edition features enabled, such as the blocks or entities specific to education edition.

fields.name: education_product_id
fields.note: EducationProductID is a UUID used to identify the education edition server instance. It is generally unique for education edition servers.

fields.name: rain_level
fields.note: RainLevel is the level specifying the intensity of the rain falling. When set to 0, no rain falls at all.

fields.name: lightning_level
fields.note: LightningLevel is the level specifying the intensity of the thunder. This may actually be set independently from the RainLevel, meaning dark clouds can be produced without rain.

fields.name: confirmed_platform_locked_content
fields.note: ConfirmedPlatformLockedContent ...

fields.name: multi_player_game
fields.note: MultiPlayerGame specifies if the world is a multi-player game. This should always be set to true for servers.

fields.name: lanbroadcast_enabled
fields.note: LANBroadcastEnabled specifies if LAN broadcast was intended to be enabled for the world.

fields.name: xblbroadcast_mode
fields.note: XBLBroadcastMode is the mode used to broadcast the joined game across XBOX Live.

fields.name: platform_broadcast_mode
fields.note: PlatformBroadcastMode is the mode used to broadcast the joined game across the platform.

fields.name: commands_enabled
fields.note: CommandsEnabled specifies if commands are enabled for the player. It is recommended to always set this to true on the server, as setting it to false means the player cannot, under any circumstance, use a command.

fields.name: texture_pack_required
fields.note: TexturePackRequired specifies if the texture pack the world might hold is required, meaning the client was forced to download it before joining.

fields.name: game_rules
fields.note: GameRules defines game rules currently active with their respective values. The value of these game rules may be either 'bool', 'int32' or 'float32'. Some game rules are server side only, and don't necessarily need to be sent to the client.

children.name: name
children.note: Name is the name of the game rule.

children.name: can_be_modified_by_player
children.note: CanBeModifiedByPlayer specifies if the game rule can be modified by the player through the in-game UI.

children.name: value
children.note: Value is the new value of the game rule. This is either a bool, uint32 or float32.

fields.name: experiments
fields.note: Experiments holds a list of experiments that are either enabled or disabled in the world that the player spawns in.

children.name: name
children.note: Name is the name of the experiment.

children.name: enabled
children.note: Enabled specifies if the experiment is enabled. Vanilla typically always sets this to true for any experiments sent.

fields.name: experiments_previously_toggled
fields.note: ExperimentsPreviouslyToggled specifies if any experiments were previously toggled in this world. It is probably used for some kind of metrics.

fields.name: bonus_chest_enabled
fields.note: BonusChestEnabled specifies if the world had the bonus map setting enabled when generating it. It does not have any effect client-side.

fields.name: start_with_map_enabled
fields.note: StartWithMapEnabled specifies if the world has the start with map setting enabled, meaning each joining player obtains a map. This should always be set to false, because the client obtains a map all on its own accord if this is set to true.

fields.name: player_permissions
fields.note: PlayerPermissions is the permission level of the player. It is a value from 0-3, with 0 being visitor, 1 being member, 2 being operator and 3 being custom.

fields.name: server_chunk_tick_radius
fields.note: ServerChunkTickRadius is the radius around the player in which chunks are ticked. Most servers set this value to a fixed number, as it does not necessarily affect anything client-side.

fields.name: has_locked_behaviour_pack
fields.note: HasLockedBehaviourPack specifies if the behaviour pack of the world is locked, meaning it cannot be disabled from the world. This is typically set for worlds on the marketplace that have a dedicated behaviour pack.

fields.name: has_locked_texture_pack
fields.note: HasLockedTexturePack specifies if the texture pack of the world is locked, meaning it cannot be disabled from the world. This is typically set for worlds on the marketplace that have a dedicated texture pack.

fields.name: from_locked_world_template
fields.note: FromLockedWorldTemplate specifies if the world from the server was from a locked world template. For servers this should always be set to false.

fields.name: msagamer_tags_only
fields.note: MSAGamerTagsOnly ..

fields.name: from_world_template
fields.note: FromWorldTemplate specifies if the world from the server was from a world template. For servers this should always be set to false.

fields.name: world_template_settings_locked
fields.note: WorldTemplateSettingsLocked specifies if the world was a template that locks all settings that change properties above in the settings GUI. It is recommended to set this to true for servers that do not allow things such as setting game rules through the GUI.

fields.name: only_spawn_v1_villagers
fields.note: OnlySpawnV1Villagers is a hack that Mojang put in place to preserve backwards compatibility with old villagers. The bool is never actually read though, so it has no functionality.

fields.name: persona_disabled
fields.note: PersonaDisabled is true if persona skins are disabled for the current game session.

fields.name: custom_skins_disabled
fields.note: CustomSkinsDisabled is true if custom skins are disabled for the current game session.

fields.name: emote_chat_muted
fields.note: EmoteChatMuted specifies if players will be sent a chat message when using certain emotes.

fields.name: base_game_version
fields.note: BaseGameVersion is the version of the game from which Vanilla features will be used. The exact function of this field isn't clear.

fields.name: new_nether
fields.note: NewNether specifies if the server runs with the new nether introduced in the 1.16 update.

fields.name: education_shared_resource_uri
fields.note: EducationSharedResourceURI is an education edition feature that transmits education resource settings to clients.

children.name: button_name
children.note: ButtonName is the button name of the resource URI.

children.name: link_uri
children.note: LinkURI is the link URI for the resource URI.

fields.name: force_experimental_gameplay
fields.note: ForceExperimentalGameplay specifies if experimental gameplay should be force enabled. For servers this should always be set to false.

fields.name: level_id
fields.note: LevelID is a base64 encoded world ID that is used to identify the world.

fields.name: world_name
fields.note: WorldName is the name of the world that the player is joining. Note that this field shows up above the player list for the rest of the game session, and cannot be changed. Setting the server name to this field is recommended.

fields.name: template_content_identity
fields.note: TemplateContentIdentity is a UUID specific to the premium world template that might have been used to generate the world. Servers should always fill out an empty string for this.

fields.name: trial
fields.note: Trial specifies if the world was a trial world, meaning features are limited and there is a time limit on the world.

fields.name: player_movement_settings
fields.note: PlayerMovementSettings ...

children.name: movement_type
children.note: MovementType is kept in-memory for legacy compatibility, but is no longer encoded in 1.21.90.

children.name: rewind_history_size
children.note: RewindHistorySize is the amount of history to keep at maximum.

children.name: server_authoritative_block_breaking
children.note: ServerAuthoritativeBlockBreaking specifies if block breaking should be sent through packet.PlayerAuthInput or not.

fields.name: time
fields.note: Time is the total time that has elapsed since the start of the world.

fields.name: enchantment_seed
fields.note: EnchantmentSeed is the seed used to seed the random used to produce enchantments in the enchantment table. Note that the exact correct random implementation must be used to produce the correct results both client- and server-side.

fields.name: blocks
fields.note: Blocks is a list of all custom blocks registered on the server.

children.name: name
children.note: Name is the name of the custom block.

children.name: properties
children.note: Properties is a list of properties which, in combination with the name, specify a unique block.

fields.name: multi_player_correlation_id
fields.note: MultiPlayerCorrelationID is a unique ID specifying the multi-player session of the player. A random UUID should be filled out for this field.

fields.name: server_authoritative_inventory
fields.note: ServerAuthoritativeInventory specifies if the server authoritative inventory system is enabled. This is a new system introduced in 1.16. Backwards compatibility with the inventory transactions has to some extent been preserved, but will eventually be removed.

fields.name: game_version
fields.note: GameVersion is the version of the game the server is running. The exact function of this field isn't clear.

fields.name: property_data
fields.note: PropertyData contains properties that should be applied on the player. These properties are the same as the ones that are sent in the SyncActorProperty packet.

fields.name: server_block_state_checksum
fields.note: ServerBlockStateChecksum is a checksum to ensure block states between the server and client match. This can simply be left empty, and the client will avoid trying to verify it.

fields.name: client_side_generation
fields.note: ClientSideGeneration is true if the client should use the features registered in the FeatureRegistry packet to generate terrain client-side to save on bandwidth.

fields.name: world_template_id
fields.note: WorldTemplateID is a UUID that identifies the template that was used to generate the world. Servers that do not use a world based off of a template can set this to an empty UUID.

fields.name: chat_restriction_level
fields.note: ChatRestrictionLevel specifies the level of restriction on in-game chat. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: disable_player_interactions
fields.note: DisablePlayerInteractions is true if the client should ignore other players when interacting with the world.

fields.name: server_id
fields.note: ServerID is always empty in vanilla and its usage is currently unknown.

fields.name: world_id
fields.note: WorldID is always empty in vanilla and its usage is currently unknown.

fields.name: scenario_id
fields.note: ScenarioID is always empty in vanilla and its usage is currently unknown.

fields.name: owner_id
fields.note: OwnerID is always empty in vanilla and its usage is currently unknown.

fields.name: use_block_network_idhashes
fields.note: UseBlockNetworkIDHashes is true if the client should use the hash of a block's name as its network ID rather than its index in the expected block palette. This is useful for servers that wish to support multiple protocol versions and custom blocks, but it will result in extra bytes being written for every block in a sub chunk palette.

fields.name: server_authoritative_sound
fields.note: ServerAuthoritativeSound is currently unknown as to what it does.

This is useful for servers that wish to support multiple protocol versions and custom blocks, but it will result in extra bytes being written for every block in a sub chunk palette. |

packets.content:
## 12 · AddPlayer · 玩家实体进入视野

- 分组：实体状态
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：用户名、UUID、runtime_id、坐标、速度、元数据、装备、能力与device_os以实际字段为准；设备ID可被客户端改变，不作可信身份。
- 本内核原始说明：AddPlayer is sent by the server to the client to make a player entity show up client-side. It is one of the few entities that cannot be sent using the AddActor packet.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `uuid` | `uuid.UUID` | UUID is the UUID of the player. It is the same UUID that the client sent in the Login packet at the start of the session. A player with this UUID must exist in the player list (built up using the PlayerList packet), for it to show up in-game. |
| `username` | `string` | Username is the name of the player. This username is the username that will be set as the initial name tag of the player. |
| `entity_runtime_id` | `uint64` | 当前会话实体运行ID，不同会话不能复用；64位ID建议传十进制字符串。 EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID. |
| `platform_chat_id` | `string` | PlatformChatID is an identifier only set for particular platforms when chatting (presumably only for Nintendo Switch). It is otherwise an empty string, and is used to decide which players are able to chat with each other. |
| `position` | `mgl32.Vec3` | 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position to spawn the player on. If the player is on a distance that the viewer cannot see it, the player will still show up if the viewer moves closer. |
| `velocity` | `mgl32.Vec3` | 协议速度向量，单位需结合游戏刻核对。 Velocity is the initial velocity the player spawns with. This velocity will initiate client side movement of the player. |
| `pitch` | `float32` | 俯仰角。 Pitch is the vertical rotation of the player. Facing straight forward yields a pitch of 0. Pitch is measured in degrees. |
| `yaw` | `float32` | 偏航角。 Yaw is the horizontal rotation of the player. Yaw is also measured in degrees. |
| `head_yaw` | `float32` | 头部偏航角。 HeadYaw is the same as Yaw, except that it applies specifically to the head of the player. A different value for HeadYaw than Yaw means that the player will have its head turned. |
| `held_item` | `protocol.ItemInstance` | HeldItem is the item that the player is holding. The item is shown to the viewer as soon as the player itself shows up. Needless to say that this field is rather pointless, as additional packets still must be sent for armour to show up. |
| `game_type` | `int32` | GameType is the game type of the player. If set to GameTypeSpectator, the player will not be shown to viewers. |
| `entity_metadata` | `map[uint32]interface {}` | EntityMetadata is a map of entity metadata, which includes flags and data properties that alter in particular the way the player looks. Flags include ones such as 'on fire' and 'sprinting'. The metadata values are indexed by their property key. |
| `entity_properties` | `protocol.EntityProperties` | EntityProperties is a list of properties that the entity inhibits. These properties define and alter specific attributes of the entity. |
| `ability_data` | `protocol.AbilityData` | AbilityData represents various data about the abilities of a player, such as ability layers or permissions. |
| `entity_links` | `[]protocol.EntityLink` | EntityLinks is a list of entity links that are currently active on the player. These links alter the way the player shows up when first spawned in terms of it shown as riding an entity. Setting these links is important for new viewers to see the player is riding another entity. |
| `device_id` | `string` | DeviceID is the device ID set in one of the files found in the storage of the device of the player. It may be changed freely, so it should not be relied on for anything. |
| `build_platform` | `int32` | BuildPlatform is the build platform/device OS of the player that is about to be added, as it sent in the Login packet when joining. |

### held_item 嵌套字段

- `stack_network_id` (`int32`)：StackNetworkID is the network ID of the item stack. If the stack is empty, 0 is always written for this field. If not, the field should be set to 1 if the server authoritative inventories are disabled in the StartGame packet, or to a unique stack ID if it is enabled.
- `stack` (`ItemStack`)：Stack is the actual item stack of the item instance.
- `stack.block_runtime_id` (`int32`)：BlockRuntimeID ...
- `stack.count` (`uint16`)：Count is the count of items that the item stack holds.
- `stack.nbtdata` (`map[string]any`)：NBTData is a map that is serialised to its NBT representation when sent in a packet.
- `stack.can_be_placed_on` (`[]string`)：CanBePlacedOn is a list of block identifiers like 'minecraft:stone' which the item, if it is an item that can be placed, can be placed on top of.
- `stack.can_break` (`[]string`)：CanBreak is a list of block identifiers like 'minecraft:dirt' that the item is able to break.
- `stack.has_network_id` (`bool`)：HasNetworkID ...

### entity_properties 嵌套字段

- `integer_properties` (`[]IntegerEntityProperty`)：IntegerProperties is a list of entity properties that contain integer values.
- `integer_properties.index` (`uint32`)：Index represents the index of the property. It is unclear what the exact purpose of this is.
- `integer_properties.value` (`int32`)：Value is the value of the property.
- `float_properties` (`[]FloatEntityProperty`)：FloatProperties is a list of entity properties that contain float values.
- `float_properties.index` (`uint32`)：Index represents the index of the property. It is unclear what the exact purpose of this is.
- `float_properties.value` (`float32`)：Value is the value of the property.

### ability_data 嵌套字段

- `entity_unique_id` (`int64`)：EntityUniqueID is a unique identifier of the player. It appears it is not required to fill this field out with a correct value. Simply writing 0 seems to work.
- `player_permissions` (`byte`)：PlayerPermissions is the permission level of the player as it shows up in the player list built up using the PlayerList packet.
- `command_permissions` (`byte`)：CommandPermissions is a set of permissions that specify what commands a player is allowed to execute.
- `layers` (`[]AbilityLayer`)：Layers contains all ability layers and their potential values. This should at least have one entry, being the base layer.
- `layers.type` (`uint16`)：Type represents the type of the layer. This is one of the AbilityLayerType constants defined above.
- `layers.abilities` (`uint32`)：Abilities is a set of abilities that are enabled for the layer. This is one of the Ability constants defined above.
- `layers.values` (`uint32`)：Values is a set of values that are associated with the enabled abilities, representing the values of the abilities.
- `layers.fly_speed` (`float32`)：FlySpeed is the default horizontal fly speed of the layer.
- `layers.vertical_fly_speed` (`float32`)：VerticalFlySpeed is the default vertical fly speed of the layer.
- `layers.walk_speed` (`float32`)：WalkSpeed is the default walk speed of the layer.

### entity_links 嵌套字段

- `ridden_entity_unique_id` (`int64`)：RiddenEntityUniqueID is the entity unique ID of the entity that is being ridden. For a player sitting in a boat, this is the unique ID of the boat.
- `rider_entity_unique_id` (`int64`)：RiderEntityUniqueID is the entity unique ID of the entity that is riding. For a player sitting in a boat, this is the unique ID of the player.
- `type` (`byte`)：Type is one of the types above. It specifies the way the entity is linked to another entity.
- `immediate` (`bool`)：Immediate is set to immediately dismount an entity from another. This should be set when the mount of an entity is killed.
- `rider_initiated` (`bool`)：RiderInitiated specifies if the link was created by the rider, for example the player starting to ride a horse by itself. This is generally true in vanilla environment for players.
- `vehicle_angular_velocity` (`float32`)：VehicleAngularVelocity is the angular velocity of the vehicle that the rider is riding.

- `immediate` (`bool`)：Immediate is set to immediately dismount an entity from another. This should be set when the mount of an entity is killed.
- `rider_initiated` (`bool`)：RiderInitiated specifies if the link was created by the rider, for example the player starting to ride a horse by itself. This is generally true in vanilla environment for players.
- `vehicle_angular_velocity` (`float32`)：VehicleAngularVelocity is the angular velocity of the vehicle that the rider is riding.

### item 嵌套字段

- `stack_network_id` (`int32`)：StackNetworkID is the network ID of the item stack. If the stack is empty, 0 is always written for this field. If not, the field should be set to 1 if the server authoritative inventories are disabled in the StartGame packet, or to a unique stack ID if it is enabled.
- `stack` (`ItemStack`)：Stack is the actual item stack of the item instance.
- `stack.block_runtime_id` (`int32`)：BlockRuntimeID ...
- `stack.count` (`uint16`)：Count is the count of items that the item stack holds.

fields.name: pitch
fields.note: 俯仰角。 Pitch is the vertical rotation of the player. Facing straight forward yields a pitch of 0. Pitch is measured in degrees.

fields.name: yaw
fields.note: 偏航角。 Yaw is the horizontal rotation of the player. Yaw is also measured in degrees.

fields.name: head_yaw
fields.note: 头部偏航角。 HeadYaw is the same as Yaw, except that it applies specifically to the head of the player. A different value for HeadYaw than Yaw means that the player will have its head turned.

fields.name: mode
fields.note: Mode is the mode of the movement. It specifies the way the player's movement should be shown to other players. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: on_ground
fields.note: OnGround specifies if the player is considered on the ground. Note that proxies or hacked clients could fake this to always be true, so it should not be taken for granted.

fields.name: ridden_entity_runtime_id
fields.note: RiddenEntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity that the player might currently be riding. If not riding, this should be left 0.

fields.name: teleport_cause
fields.note: TeleportCause is written only if Mode is MoveModeTeleport. It specifies the cause of the teleportation, which is one of the constants above.

fields.name: teleport_source_entity_type
fields.note: TeleportSourceEntityType is the entity type that caused the teleportation, for example an ender pearl.

fields.name: tick
fields.note: 输入/同步的游戏刻编号。 Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to CorrectPlayerMovePrediction.

packets.usage: 用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
packets.description: SetActorData is sent by the server to update the entity metadata of an entity. It includes flags such as if the entity is on fire, but also properties such as the air it has left until it starts drowning.
packets.content:
## 39 · SetActorData · 设置实体数据

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
- 本内核原始说明：SetActorData is sent by the server to update the entity metadata of an entity. It includes flags such as if the entity is on fire, but also properties such as the air it has left until it starts drowning.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `entity_runtime_id` | `uint64` | 当前会话实体运行ID，不同会话不能复用；64位ID建议传十进制字符串。 EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID. |
| `entity_metadata` | `map[uint32]interface {}` | EntityMetadata is a map of entity metadata, which includes flags and data properties that alter in particular the way the entity looks. Flags include ones such as 'on fire' and 'sprinting'. The metadata values are indexed by their property key. |
| `entity_properties` | `protocol.EntityProperties` | EntityProperties is a list of properties that the entity inhibits. These properties define and alter specific attributes of the entity. |
| `tick` | `uint64` | 输入/同步的游戏刻编号。 Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to CorrectPlayerMovePrediction. |

### entity_properties 嵌套字段

- `integer_properties` (`[]IntegerEntityProperty`)：IntegerProperties is a list of entity properties that contain integer values.
- `integer_properties.index` (`uint32`)：Index represents the index of the property. It is unclear what the exact purpose of this is.
- `integer_properties.value` (`int32`)：Value is the value of the property.
- `float_properties` (`[]FloatEntityProperty`)：FloatProperties is a list of entity properties that contain float values.
- `float_properties.index` (`uint32`)：Index represents the index of the property. It is unclear what the exact purpose of this is.
- `float_properties.value` (`float32`)：Value is the value of the property.

fields.name: entity_link
fields.note: EntityLink is the link to be set client-side. It links two entities together, so that one entity rides another. Note that players that see those entities later will not see the link, unless it is also sent in the AddActor and AddPlayer packets.

children.name: ridden_entity_unique_id
children.note: RiddenEntityUniqueID is the entity unique ID of the entity that is being ridden. For a player sitting in a boat, this is the unique ID of the boat.

children.name: rider_entity_unique_id
children.note: RiderEntityUniqueID is the entity unique ID of the entity that is riding. For a player sitting in a boat, this is the unique ID of the player.

children.name: type
children.note: Type is one of the types above. It specifies the way the entity is linked to another entity.

children.name: immediate
children.note: Immediate is set to immediately dismount an entity from another. This should be set when the mount of an entity is killed.

children.name: rider_initiated
children.note: RiderInitiated specifies if the link was created by the rider, for example the player starting to ride a horse by itself. This is generally true in vanilla environment for players.

children.name: vehicle_angular_velocity
children.note: VehicleAngularVelocity is the angular velocity of the vehicle that the rider is riding.

packets.description: SetActorLink is sent by the server to initiate an entity link client-side, meaning one entity will start riding another.
packets.content:
## 41 · SetActorLink · 设置实体关联

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
- 本内核原始说明：SetActorLink is sent by the server to initiate an entity link client-side, meaning one entity will start riding another.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `entity_link` | `protocol.EntityLink` | EntityLink is the link to be set client-side. It links two entities together, so that one entity rides another. Note that players that see those entities later will not see the link, unless it is also sent in the AddActor and AddPlayer packets. |

### entity_link 嵌套字段

- `ridden_entity_unique_id` (`int64`)：RiddenEntityUniqueID is the entity unique ID of the entity that is being ridden. For a player sitting in a boat, this is the unique ID of the boat.
- `rider_entity_unique_id` (`int64`)：RiderEntityUniqueID is the entity unique ID of the entity that is riding. For a player sitting in a boat, this is the unique ID of the player.
- `type` (`byte`)：Type is one of the types above. It specifies the way the entity is linked to another entity.
- `immediate` (`bool`)：Immediate is set to immediately dismount an entity from another. This should be set when the mount of an entity is killed.
- `rider_initiated` (`bool`)：RiderInitiated specifies if the link was created by the rider, for example the player starting to ride a horse by itself. This is generally true in vanilla environment for players.
- `vehicle_angular_velocity` (`float32`)：VehicleAngularVelocity is the angular velocity of the vehicle that the rider is riding.

fields.name: spawn_type
fields.note: SpawnType is the type of spawn to set. It is either SpawnTypePlayer or SpawnTypeWorld, and specifies the behaviour of the spawn set. If SpawnTypeWorld is set, the position to which compasses will point is also changed.

fields.name: position
fields.note: 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the new position of the spawn that was set. If SpawnType is SpawnTypeWorld, compasses will point to this position. As of 1.16, Position is always the position of the player.

fields.name: dimension
fields.note: Dimension is the ID of the dimension that had its spawn updated. This is specifically relevant for behaviour added in 1.16 such as the respawn anchor, which allows setting the spawn in a specific dimension.

fields.name: spawn_position
fields.note: SpawnPosition is a new field added in 1.16. It holds the spawn position of the world. This spawn position is {-2147483648, -2147483648, -2147483648} for a default spawn position.

packets.name: Respawn
packets.title: 重生状态同步
packets.usage: 处理ready状态，旧血量失效后等待新属性；不因重生包推算满血。
packets.description: Respawn is sent by the server to make a player respawn client-side. It is sent in response to a PlayerAction packet with ActionType PlayerActionRespawn. As of 1.13, the server sends two of these packets with different states, and the client sends one of these back in order to complete the respawn.
packets.content:
## 45 · Respawn · 重生状态同步

- 分组：属性与状态
- 方向：双向
- 用法与边界：处理ready状态，旧血量失效后等待新属性；不因重生包推算满血。
- 本内核原始说明：Respawn is sent by the server to make a player respawn client-side. It is sent in response to a PlayerAction packet with ActionType PlayerActionRespawn. As of 1.13, the server sends two of these packets with different states, and the client sends one of these back in order to complete the respawn.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `position` | `mgl32.Vec3` | 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position on which the player should be respawned. The position might be in a different dimension, in which case the client should first be sent a ChangeDimension packet. |
| `state` | `uint8` | State is the 'state' of the respawn. It is one of the constants that may be found above, and the value the packet contains depends on whether the server or client sends it. |
| `entity_runtime_id` | `uint64` | 当前会话实体运行ID，不同会话不能复用；64位ID建议传十进制字符串。 EntityRuntimeID is the entity runtime ID of the player that the respawn packet concerns. This is apparently for the server to recognise which player sends this packet. |

fields.name: window_id
fields.note: 当前容器窗口ID。 WindowID is the ID representing the window that is being opened. It may be used later to close the container using a ContainerClose packet.

fields.name: container_type
fields.note: ContainerType is the type ID of the container that is being opened when opening the container at the position of the packet. It depends on the block/entity, and could, for example, be the window type of a chest or a hopper, but also a horse inventory.

fields.name: container_position
fields.note: ContainerPosition is the position of the container opened. The position must point to a block entity that actually has a container. If that is not the case, the window will not be opened and the packet will be ignored, if a valid ContainerEntityUniqueID has not also been provided.

fields.name: container_entity_unique_id
fields.note: ContainerEntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity container that was opened. It is only used if the ContainerType is one that points to an entity, for example a horse.

packets.name: ContainerOpen
packets.title: 本机打开容器
packets.usage: 容器ID/类型/位置与实体ID；打开他人的私有箱子需服务端允许。
packets.description: ContainerOpen is sent by the server to open a container client-side. This container must be physically present in the world, for the packet to have any effect. Unlike Java Edition, Bedrock Edition requires that chests for example must be present and in range to open its inventory.
packets.content:
## 46 · ContainerOpen · 本机打开容器

- 分组：物品与容器
- 方向：服务器→本机客户端
- 用法与边界：容器ID/类型/位置与实体ID；打开他人的私有箱子需服务端允许。
- 本内核原始说明：ContainerOpen is sent by the server to open a container client-side. This container must be physically present in the world, for the packet to have any effect. Unlike Java Edition, Bedrock Edition requires that chests for example must be present and in range to open its inventory.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | `uint8` | 当前容器窗口ID。 WindowID is the ID representing the window that is being opened. It may be used later to close the container using a ContainerClose packet. |
| `container_type` | `uint8` | ContainerType is the type ID of the container that is being opened when opening the container at the position of the packet. It depends on the block/entity, and could, for example, be the window type of a chest or a hopper, but also a horse inventory. |
| `container_position` | `protocol.BlockPos` | ContainerPosition is the position of the container opened. The position must point to a block entity that actually has a container. If that is not the case, the window will not be opened and the packet will be ignored, if a valid ContainerEntityUniqueID has not also been provided. |
| `container_entity_unique_id` | `int64` | ContainerEntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity container that was opened. It is only used if the ContainerType is one that points to an entity, for example a horse. |

fields.name: window_id
fields.note: 当前容器窗口ID。 WindowID is the ID representing the window of the container that should be closed. It must be equal to the one sent in the ContainerOpen packet to close the designated window.

fields.name: container_type
fields.note: ContainerType is the type of container that the server is trying to close. This is used to validate on the client side whether or not the server's close request is valid.

fields.name: server_side
fields.note: ServerSide determines whether or not the container was force-closed by the server. If this value is not set correctly, the client may ignore the packet and respond with a PacketViolationWarning.

packets.name: ContainerClose
packets.title: 关闭容器
packets.usage: 关闭当前本机窗口；不能任意关闭别人的容器。
packets.description: ContainerClose is sent by the server to close a container the player currently has opened, which was opened using the ContainerOpen packet, or by the client to tell the server it closed a particular container, such as the crafting grid.
packets.content:

packets.title: 容器完整内容
packets.usage: 收到的容器内容，可实现自己已打开容器的菜单观测；不是所有玩家所有箱子。
packets.description: InventoryContent is sent by the server to update the full content of a particular inventory. It is usually sent for the main inventory of the player, but also works for other inventories that are currently opened by the player.
packets.content:
## 49 · InventoryContent · 容器完整内容

- 分组：物品与容器
- 方向：服务器→本机客户端
- 用法与边界：收到的容器内容，可实现自己已打开容器的菜单观测；不是所有玩家所有箱子。
- 本内核原始说明：InventoryContent is sent by the server to update the full content of a particular inventory. It is usually sent for the main inventory of the player, but also works for other inventories that are currently opened by the player.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | `uint32` | 当前容器窗口ID。 WindowID is the ID that identifies one of the windows that the client currently has opened, or one of the consistent windows such as the main inventory. |
| `content` | `[]protocol.ItemInstance` | Content is the new content of the inventory. The length of this slice must be equal to the full size of the inventory window updated. |
| `container` | `protocol.FullContainerName` | Container is the protocol.FullContainerName that describes the container that the content is for. |
| `storage_item` | `protocol.ItemInstance` | StorageItem is the item that is acting as the storage container for the inventory. If the inventory is not a dynamic container then this field should be left empty. When set, only the item type is used by the client and none of the other stack info. |

### content 嵌套字段

- `stack_network_id` (`int32`)：StackNetworkID is the network ID of the item stack. If the stack is empty, 0 is always written for this field. If not, the field should be set to 1 if the server authoritative inventories are disabled in the StartGame packet, or to a unique stack ID if it is enabled.
- `stack` (`ItemStack`)：Stack is the actual item stack of the item instance.
- `stack.block_runtime_id` (`int32`)：BlockRuntimeID ...
- `stack.count` (`uint16`)：Count is the count of items that the item stack holds.
- `stack.nbtdata` (`map[string]any`)：NBTData is a map that is serialised to its NBT representation when sent in a packet.
- `stack.can_be_placed_on` (`[]string`)：CanBePlacedOn is a list of block identifiers like 'minecraft:stone' which the item, if it is an item that can be placed, can be placed on top of.
- `stack.can_break` (`[]string`)：CanBreak is a list of block identifiers like 'minecraft:dirt' that the item is able to break.
- `stack.has_network_id` (`bool`)：HasNetworkID ...

### container 嵌套字段

- `container_id` (`byte`)：ContainerID is the ID of the container that the slot was in.
- `dynamic_container_id` (`Optional[uint32]`)：DynamicContainerID is the ID of the container if it is dynamic. If the container is not dynamic, this field should be left empty. A non-optional value of 0 is assumed to be non-empty.

### storage_item 嵌套字段

- `stack_network_id` (`int32`)：StackNetworkID is the network ID of the item stack. If the stack is empty, 0 is always written for this field. If not, the field should be set to 1 if the server authoritative inventories are disabled in the StartGame packet, or to a unique stack ID if it is enabled.
- `stack` (`ItemStack`)：Stack is the actual item stack of the item instance.
- `stack.block_runtime_id` (`int32`)：BlockRuntimeID ...
- `stack.count` (`uint16`)：Count is the count of items that the item stack holds.
- `stack.nbtdata` (`map[string]any`)：NBTData is a map that is serialised to its NBT representation when sent in a packet.
- `stack.can_be_placed_on` (`[]string`)：CanBePlacedOn is a list of block identifiers like 'minecraft:stone' which the item, if it is an item that can be placed, can be placed on top of.
- `stack.can_break` (`[]string`)：CanBreak is a list of block identifiers like 'minecraft:dirt' that the item is able to break.
- `stack.has_network_id` (`bool`)：HasNetworkID ...

## 51 · ContainerSetData · 容器设置数据

- 分组：其他协议功能

- 本内核原始说明：ContainerSetData is sent by the server to update specific data of a single container, meaning a block such as a furnace or a brewing stand. This data is usually used by the client to display certain features client-side.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |

fields.name: recipes
fields.note: Recipes is a list of all recipes available on the server. It includes among others shapeless, shaped and furnace recipes. The client will only be able to craft these recipes.

fields.name: potion_recipes
fields.note: PotionRecipes is a list of all potion mixing recipes which may be used in the brewing stand.

children.name: input_potion_id
children.note: InputPotionID is the item ID of the potion to be put in.

children.name: input_potion_metadata
children.note: InputPotionMetadata is the type of the potion to be put in. This is typically the meta of the awkward potion (or water bottle to create an awkward potion).

children.name: reagent_item_id
children.note: ReagentItemID is the item ID of the item that needs to be added to the brewing stand in order to brew the output potion.

children.name: reagent_item_metadata
children.note: ReagentItemMetadata is the metadata value of the item that needs to be added to the brewing stand in order to brew the output potion.

children.name: output_potion_id
children.note: OutputPotionID is the item ID of the potion obtained as a result of the brewing recipe.

children.name: output_potion_metadata
children.note: OutputPotionMetadata is the type of the potion that is obtained as a result of brewing the input potion with the reagent item.

fields.name: potion_container_change_recipes
fields.note: PotionContainerChangeRecipes is a list of all recipes to convert a potion from one type to another, such as from a drinkable potion to a splash potion, or from a splash potion to a lingering potion.

children.name: input_item_id
children.note: InputItemID is the item ID of the item to be put in. This is typically either the ID of a normal potion or a splash potion.

children.name: reagent_item_id
children.note: ReagentItemID is the item ID of the item that needs to be added to the container in order to create the output item.

children.name: output_item_id
children.note: OutputItemID is the item that is created using a combination of the InputItem and ReagentItem, which is typically either the ID of a splash potion or a lingering potion.

fields.name: material_reducers
fields.note: MaterialReducers is a list of all material reducers which is used in education edition chemistry.

children.name: input_item
children.note: InputItem is the starting item.

children.name: network_id
children.note: NetworkID is the numerical network ID of the item. This is sometimes a positive ID, and sometimes a negative ID, depending on what item it concerns.

children.name: metadata_value
children.note: MetadataValue is the metadata value of the item. For some items, this is the damage value, whereas for other items it is simply an identifier of a variant of the item.

children.name: outputs
children.note: Outputs contain all outputting items.

children.name: network_id
children.note: NetworkID is the network ID of the output.

children.name: count
children.note: Count is the quantity of the output.

fields.name: clear_recipes
fields.note: ClearRecipes indicates if all recipes currently active on the client should be cleaned. Doing this means that the client will have no recipes active by itself: Any CraftingData packets previously sent will also be discarded, and only the recipes in this CraftingData packet will be used.

packets.name: CraftingData
packets.title: 合成数据
packets.usage: 用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
packets.description: CraftingData is sent by the server to let the client know all crafting data that the server maintains. This includes shapeless crafting, crafting table recipes, furnace recipes etc. Each crafting station's recipes are included in it.
packets.content:
## 52 · CraftingData · 合成数据

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
- 本内核原始说明：CraftingData is sent by the server to let the client know all crafting data that the server maintains. This includes shapeless crafting, crafting table recipes, furnace recipes etc. Each crafting station's recipes are included in it.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `recipes` | `[]protocol.Recipe` | Recipes is a list of all recipes available on the server. It includes among others shapeless, shaped and furnace recipes. The client will only be able to craft these recipes. |
| `potion_recipes` | `[]protocol.PotionRecipe` | PotionRecipes is a list of all potion mixing recipes which may be used in the brewing stand. |
| `potion_container_change_recipes` | `[]protocol.PotionContainerChangeRecipe` | PotionContainerChangeRecipes is a list of all recipes to convert a potion from one type to another, such as from a drinkable potion to a splash potion, or from a splash potion to a lingering potion. |
| `material_reducers` | `[]protocol.MaterialReducer` | MaterialReducers is a list of all material reducers which is used in education edition chemistry. |
| `clear_recipes` | `bool` | ClearRecipes indicates if all recipes currently active on the client should be cleaned. Doing this means that the client will have no recipes active by itself: Any CraftingData packets previously sent will also be discarded, and only the recipes in this CraftingData packet will be used. |

### potion_recipes 嵌套字段

- `input_potion_id` (`int32`)：InputPotionID is the item ID of the potion to be put in.
- `input_potion_metadata` (`int32`)：InputPotionMetadata is the type of the potion to be put in. This is typically the meta of the awkward potion (or water bottle to create an awkward potion).
- `reagent_item_id` (`int32`)：ReagentItemID is the item ID of the item that needs to be added to the brewing stand in order to brew the output potion.
- `reagent_item_metadata` (`int32`)：ReagentItemMetadata is the metadata value of the item that needs to be added to the brewing stand in order to brew the output potion.
- `output_potion_id` (`int32`)：OutputPotionID is the item ID of the potion obtained as a result of the brewing recipe.
- `output_potion_metadata` (`int32`)：OutputPotionMetadata is the type of the potion that is obtained as a result of brewing the input potion with the reagent item.

### potion_container_change_recipes 嵌套字段

- `input_item_id` (`int32`)：InputItemID is the item ID of the item to be put in. This is typically either the ID of a normal potion or a splash potion.
- `reagent_item_id` (`int32`)：ReagentItemID is the item ID of the item that needs to be added to the container in order to create the output item.
- `output_item_id` (`int32`)：OutputItemID is the item that is created using a combination of the InputItem and ReagentItem, which is typically either the ID of a splash potion or a lingering potion.

### material_reducers 嵌套字段

- `input_item` (`ItemType`)：InputItem is the starting item.
- `input_item.network_id` (`int32`)：NetworkID is the numerical network ID of the item. This is sometimes a positive ID, and sometimes a negative ID, depending on what item it concerns.
- `input_item.metadata_value` (`uint32`)：MetadataValue is the metadata value of the item. For some items, this is the damage value, whereas for other items it is simply an identifier of a variant of the item.
- `outputs` (`[]MaterialReducerOutput`)：Outputs contain all outputting items.
- `outputs.network_id` (`int32`)：NetworkID is the network ID of the output.
- `outputs.count` (`int32`)：Count is the quantity of the output.

packets.name: AdventureSettings
packets.title: 冒险模式与权限设置
packets.usage: 旧协议的权限和能力位，不能靠修改包取得服务器权限。
packets.description: AdventureSettings is sent by the server to update game-play related features, in particular permissions to access these features for the client. It includes allowing the player to fly, build and mine, and attack entities. Most of these flags should be checked server-side instead of using this packet only. The client may also send this packet to the server when it updates one of these settings through the in-game settings interface. The server should verify if the player actually has permission to update those settings.
packets.content:
## 55 · AdventureSettings · 冒险模式与权限设置

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：旧协议的权限和能力位，不能靠修改包取得服务器权限。
- 本内核原始说明：AdventureSettings is sent by the server to update game-play related features, in particular permissions to access these features for the client. It includes allowing the player to fly, build and mine, and attack entities. Most of these flags should be checked server-side instead of using this packet only. The client may also send this packet to the server when it updates one of these settings through the in-game settings interface. The server should verify if the player actually has permission to update those settings.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `flags` | `uint32` | Flags is a set of flags that specify certain properties of the player, such as whether or not it can fly and/or move through blocks. It is one of the AdventureFlag constants above. |
| `command_permission_level` | `uint32` | CommandPermissionLevel is a permission level that specifies the kind of commands that the player is allowed to use. It is one of the CommandPermissionLevel constants above. |
| `action_permissions` | `uint32` | ActionPermissions is, much like Flags, a set of flags that specify actions that the player is allowed to undertake, such as whether it is allowed to edit blocks, open doors etc. It is a combination of the ActionPermission constants above. |
| `permission_level` | `uint32` | PermissionLevel is the permission level of the player as it shows up in the player list built up using the PlayerList packet. It is one of the PermissionLevel constants above. |
| `custom_stored_permissions` | `uint32` | CustomStoredPermissions ... |
| `player_unique_id` | `int64` | PlayerUniqueID is a unique identifier of the player. This must be filled out with the entity unique ID of the player. |

fields.name: position
fields.note: 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position of the block that holds the block entity. If no block entity is at this position, the packet is ignored by the client.

fields.name: nbtdata
fields.note: NBTData is the new data of the block that will be encoded to NBT and applied client-side, so that the client can see the block update. The NBTData should contain all properties of the block, not just properties that were changed.

- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
- 本内核原始说明：BlockActorData is sent by the server to update data of a block entity client-side, for example the data of a chest.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `position` | `protocol.BlockPos` | 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position of the block that holds the block entity. If no block entity is at this position, the packet is ignored by the client. |
| `nbtdata` | `map[string]interface {}` | NBTData is the new data of the block that will be encoded to NBT and applied client-side, so that the client can see the block update. The NBTData should contain all properties of the block, not just properties that were changed. |

fields.name: position
fields.note: 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position contains the X and Z coordinates of the chunk sent. You can convert a block coordinate to a chunk coordinate by right-shifting it four bits.

fields.name: dimension
fields.note: Dimension is the ID of the dimension that the chunk belongs to. This must always be set otherwise the client will always assume the chunk is part of the overworld dimension.

fields.name: highest_sub_chunk
fields.note: HighestSubChunk is the highest sub-chunk at the position that is not all air. It is only set if the SubChunkCount is set to protocol.SubChunkRequestModeLimited.

fields.name: sub_chunk_count
fields.note: SubChunkCount is the amount of sub-chunks that are part of the chunk sent. Depending on if the cache is enabled, a list of blob hashes will be sent, or, if disabled, the sub-chunk data. SubChunkCount may be set to protocol.SubChunkRequestModeLimited or protocol.SubChunkRequestModeLimitless to prompt the client to send a SubChunkRequest in response. If this field is set to protocol.SubChunkRequestModeLimited, HighestSubChunk is used.

fields.name: cache_enabled
fields.note: CacheEnabled specifies if the client blob cache should be enabled. This system is based on hashes of blobs which are consistent and saved by the client in combination with that blob, so that the server does not have the same chunk multiple times. If the client does not yet have a blob with the hash sent, it will send a ClientCacheBlobStatus packet containing the hashes is does not have the data of.

fields.name: blob_hashes
fields.note: BlobHashes is a list of all blob hashes used in the chunk. It is composed of SubChunkCount + 1 hashes, with the first SubChunkCount hashes being those of the sub-chunks and the last one that of the biome of the chunk. If CacheEnabled is set to false, BlobHashes can be left empty.

fields.name: raw_payload
fields.note: RawPayload is a serialised string of chunk data. The data held depends on if CacheEnabled is set to true. If set to false, the payload is composed of multiple sub-chunks, each of which carry a version which indicates the way they are serialised, followed by biomes, border blocks and tile entities. If CacheEnabled is true, the payload consists out of the border blocks and tile entities only.

packets.name: LevelChunk
packets.title: 整块区块数据
packets.usage: 完整区块解析涉及压缩、调色板与子区块。当前world.blockState仅最近UpdateBlock观测，不宣称完整世界缓存或寻路已做完。
packets.description: LevelChunk is sent by the server to provide the client with a chunk of a world data (16xYx16 blocks). Typically, a certain amount of chunks is sent to the client before sending it the spawn PlayStatus packet, so that the client spawns in a loaded world.
packets.content:

- 方向：服务器→客户端

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `position` | `protocol.ChunkPos` | 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position contains the X and Z coordinates of the chunk sent. You can convert a block coordinate to a chunk coordinate by right-shifting it four bits. |
| `dimension` | `int32` | Dimension is the ID of the dimension that the chunk belongs to. This must always be set otherwise the client will always assume the chunk is part of the overworld dimension. |
| `highest_sub_chunk` | `uint16` | HighestSubChunk is the highest sub-chunk at the position that is not all air. It is only set if the SubChunkCount is set to protocol.SubChunkRequestModeLimited. |
| `sub_chunk_count` | `uint32` | SubChunkCount is the amount of sub-chunks that are part of the chunk sent. Depending on if the cache is enabled, a list of blob hashes will be sent, or, if disabled, the sub-chunk data. SubChunkCount may be set to protocol.SubChunkRequestModeLimited or protocol.SubChunkRequestModeLimitless to prompt the client to send a SubChunkRequest in response. If this field is set to protocol.SubChunkRequestModeLimited, HighestSubChunk is used. |
| `cache_enabled` | `bool` | CacheEnabled specifies if the client blob cache should be enabled. This system is based on hashes of blobs which are consistent and saved by the client in combination with that blob, so that the server does not have the same chunk multiple times. If the client does not yet have a blob with the hash sent, it will send a ClientCacheBlobStatus packet containing the hashes is does not have the data of. |
| `blob_hashes` | `[]uint64` | BlobHashes is a list of all blob hashes used in the chunk. It is composed of SubChunkCount + 1 hashes, with the first SubChunkCount hashes being those of the sub-chunks and the last one that of the biome of the chunk. If CacheEnabled is set to false, BlobHashes can be left empty. |
| `raw_payload` | `[]uint8` | RawPayload is a serialised string of chunk data. The data held depends on if CacheEnabled is set to true. If set to false, the payload is composed of multiple sub-chunks, each of which carry a version which indicates the way they are serialised, followed by biomes, border blocks and tile entities. If CacheEnabled is true, the payload consists out of the border blocks and tile entities only. |

fields.name: dimension
fields.note: Dimension is the dimension that the client should be changed to. The fog colour will change depending on the type of dimension, which is one of the constants above. Note that Dimension MUST be a different dimension than the one that the player is currently in. Sending a ChangeDimension packet with a Dimension that the player is currently in will result in a never-ending dimension change screen.

fields.name: position
fields.note: 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position in the new dimension that the player is spawned in.

fields.name: respawn
fields.note: Respawn specifies if the dimension change was respawn based, meaning that the player died in one dimension and got respawned into another. The client will send a PlayerAction packet with PlayerActionDimensionChangeRequest if it dies in another dimension, indicating that it needs a DimensionChange packet with Respawn set to true.

fields.name: loading_screen_id
fields.note: LoadingScreenID is a unique ID for the loading screen that the player is currently in. The client will update the server on its state through the ServerBoundLoadingScreen packet, and it can be used to not send specific packets to the client if it is changing dimensions. This field should be unique for every ChangeDimension packet sent.

packets.name: ChangeDimension
packets.title: 切换维度
packets.usage: 维度与传送位置改变，应清除旧维度位置缓存。
packets.description: ChangeDimension is sent by the server to the client to send a dimension change screen client-side. Once the screen is cleared client-side, the client will send a PlayerAction packet with PlayerActionDimensionChangeDone.
packets.content:
## 61 · ChangeDimension · 切换维度

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：维度与传送位置改变，应清除旧维度位置缓存。
- 本内核原始说明：ChangeDimension is sent by the server to the client to send a dimension change screen client-side. Once the screen is cleared client-side, the client will send a PlayerAction packet with PlayerActionDimensionChangeDone.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `dimension` | `int32` | Dimension is the dimension that the client should be changed to. The fog colour will change depending on the type of dimension, which is one of the constants above. Note that Dimension MUST be a different dimension than the one that the player is currently in. Sending a ChangeDimension packet with a Dimension that the player is currently in will result in a never-ending dimension change screen. |
| `position` | `mgl32.Vec3` | 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position in the new dimension that the player is spawned in. |
| `respawn` | `bool` | Respawn specifies if the dimension change was respawn based, meaning that the player died in one dimension and got respawned into another. The client will send a PlayerAction packet with PlayerActionDimensionChangeRequest if it dies in another dimension, indicating that it needs a DimensionChange packet with Respawn set to true. |
| `loading_screen_id` | `protocol.Optional[uint32]` | LoadingScreenID is a unique ID for the loading screen that the player is currently in. The client will update the server on its state through the ServerBoundLoadingScreen packet, and it can be used to not send specific packets to the client if it is changing dimensions. This field should be unique for every ChangeDimension packet sent. |

fields.name: game_type
fields.note: GameType is the new game type of the player. It is one of the constants that can be found above. Some of these game types require additional flags to be set in an AdventureSettings packet for the game mode to obtain its full functionality.
