fields.name: action_type
fields.note: 动作枚举，具体编号使用本内核定义。 ActionType is the action to execute upon the player list. The entries that follow specify which entries are added or removed from the player list.

fields.name: entries
fields.note: Entries is a list of all player list entries that should be added/removed from the player list, depending on the ActionType set.

children.name: uuid
children.note: UUID is the UUID of the player as sent in the Login packet when the client joined the server. It must match this UUID exactly for the correct XBOX Live icon to show up in the list.

children.name: entity_unique_id
children.note: EntityUniqueID is the unique entity ID of the player. This ID typically stays consistent during the lifetime of a world, but servers often send the runtime ID for this.

children.name: username
children.note: Username is the username that is shown in the player list of the player that obtains a PlayerList packet with this entry. It does not have to be the same as the actual username of the player.

children.name: xuid
children.note: XUID is the XBOX Live user ID of the player, which will remain consistent as long as the player is logged in with the XBOX Live account.

children.name: platform_chat_id
children.note: PlatformChatID is an identifier only set for particular platforms when chatting (presumably only for Nintendo Switch). It is otherwise an empty string, and is used to decide which players are able to chat with each other.

children.name: build_platform
children.note: BuildPlatform is the platform of the player as sent by that player in the Login packet.

children.name: skin
children.note: Skin is the skin of the player that should be added to the player list. Once sent here, it will not have to be sent again.

children.name: skin_id
children.note: SkinID is a unique ID produced for the skin, for example 'c18e65aa-7b21-4637-9b63-8ad63622ef01_Alex' for the default Alex skin.

children.name: play_fab_id
children.note: PlayFabID is the PlayFab ID produced for the skin. PlayFab is the company that hosts the Marketplace, skins and other related features from the game. This ID is the ID of the skin used to store the skin inside of PlayFab.

children.name: skin_resource_patch
children.note: SkinResourcePatch is a JSON encoded object holding some fields that point to the geometry that the skin has. The JSON object that this holds specifies the way that the geometry of animations and the default skin of the player are combined.

children.name: skin_data
children.note: SkinData is a byte slice of SkinImageWidth * SkinImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte representation of the skin pixels.

children.name: animations
children.note: Animations is a list of all animations that the skin has.

children.name: image_data
children.note: ImageData is a byte slice of ImageWidth * ImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte representation of the animation image pixels. The ImageData contains FrameCount images in it, which each represent one stage of the animation. The actual part of the skin that this field holds depends on the AnimationType, where SkinAnimationHead holds only the head and its hat, whereas the other animations hold the entire body of the skin.

children.name: animation_type
children.note: AnimationType is the type of the animation, which is one of the types found above. The data that ImageData contains depends on this type.

children.name: frame_count
children.note: FrameCount is the amount of frames that the skin animation holds. The number of frames here is the amount of images that may be found in the ImageData field.

children.name: expression_type
children.note: ExpressionType is the type of expression made by the skin, which is one the types found above.

children.name: cape_data
children.note: CapeData is a byte slice of 64*32*4 bytes. It is a RGBA ordered byte representation of the cape colours, much like the SkinData.

children.name: skin_geometry
children.note: SkinGeometry is a JSON encoded structure of the geometry data of a skin, containing properties such as bones, uv, pivot etc.

children.name: animation_data
children.note: TODO: Find out what value AnimationData holds and when it does hold something.

children.name: geometry_data_engine_version
children.note: GeometryDataEngineVersion ...

children.name: premium_skin
children.note: PremiumSkin specifies if this is a skin that was purchased from the marketplace.

children.name: persona_skin
children.note: PersonaSkin specifies if this is a skin that was created using the in-game skin creator.

children.name: persona_cape_on_classic_skin
children.note: PersonaCapeOnClassicSkin specifies if the skin had a Persona cape (in-game skin creator cape) equipped on a classic skin.

children.name: primary_user
children.note: PrimaryUser ...

children.name: cape_id
children.note: CapeID is a unique identifier that identifies the cape. It usually holds a UUID in it.

children.name: full_id
children.note: FullID is an ID that represents the skin in full. The actual functionality is unknown: The client does not seem to send a value for this.

children.name: skin_colour
children.note: SkinColour is a hex representation (including #) of the base colour of the skin. An example of the colour sent here is '#b37b62'.

children.name: arm_size
children.note: ArmSize is the size of the arms of the player's model. This is either 'wide' (generally for male skins) or 'slim' (generally for female skins).

children.name: persona_pieces
children.note: PersonaPieces is a list of all persona pieces that the skin is composed of.

children.name: piece_id
children.note: PieceId is a UUID that identifies the piece itself, which is unique for each separate piece.

children.name: piece_type
children.note: PieceType holds the type of the piece. Several types I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_skeleton - persona_body - persona_skin - persona_bottom - persona_feet - persona_top - persona_mouth - persona_hair - persona_eyes - persona_facial_hair

children.name: pack_id
children.note: PackID is a UUID that identifies the pack that the persona piece belongs to.

children.name: default
children.note: Default specifies if the piece is one of the default pieces. This is true when the piece is one of those that a Steve or Alex skin have.

children.name: product_id
children.note: ProductID is a UUID that identifies the piece when it comes to purchases. It is empty for pieces that have the 'Default' field set to true.

children.name: piece_tint_colours
children.note: PieceTintColours is a list of specific tint colours for (some of) the persona pieces found in the list above.

children.name: piece_type
children.note: PieceType is the type of the persona skin piece that this tint colour concerns. The piece type must always be present in the persona pieces list, but not each piece type has a tint colour sent. Pieces that do have a tint colour that I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_mouth - persona_eyes - persona_hair

children.name: colours
children.note: Colours is a list four colours written in hex notation (note, that unlike the SkinColour field in the ClientData struct, this is actually ARGB, not just RGB). The colours refer to different parts of the skin piece. The 'persona_eyes' may have the following colours: ["#ffa12722","#ff2f1f0f","#ff3aafd9","#0"] The first hex colour represents the tint colour of the iris, the second hex colour represents the eyebrows and the third represents the sclera. The fourth is #0 because there are only 3 parts of the persona_eyes skin piece.

children.name: trusted
children.note: Trusted specifies if the skin is 'trusted'. No code should rely on this field, as any proxy or client can easily change it.

children.name: override_appearance
children.note: OverrideAppearance specifies if the skin should override the player's skin that is equipped client-side. When false, the client will reject the skin and continue to use the skin that the player has equipped.

children.name: teacher
children.note: Teacher is a Minecraft: Education Edition field. It specifies if the player to be added to the player list is a teacher.

children.name: host
children.note: Host specifies if the player that is added to the player list is the host of the game.

children.name: sub_client
children.note: SubClient specifies if the player that is added to the player list is a sub-client of another player.

children.name: player_colour
children.note: PlayerColour is the colour of the player that is shown in UI elements, currently only used for the player locator bar.

packets.name: PlayerList
packets.title: 玩家名单变更
packets.usage: 玩家加入/移除列表、UUID和皮肤资料；在线名单与皮肤缓存入口。
packets.description: PlayerList is sent by the server to update the client-side player list in the in-game menu screen. It shows the icon of each player if the correct XUID is written in the packet. Sending the PlayerList packet is obligatory when sending an AddPlayer packet. The added player will not show up to a client if it has not been added to the player list, because several properties of the player are obtained from the player list, such as the skin.
packets.content:
## 63 · PlayerList · 玩家名单变更

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：玩家加入/移除列表、UUID和皮肤资料；在线名单与皮肤缓存入口。
- 本内核原始说明：PlayerList is sent by the server to update the client-side player list in the in-game menu screen. It shows the icon of each player if the correct XUID is written in the packet. Sending the PlayerList packet is obligatory when sending an AddPlayer packet. The added player will not show up to a client if it has not been added to the player list, because several properties of the player are obtained from the player list, such as the skin.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `action_type` | `uint8` | 动作枚举，具体编号使用本内核定义。 ActionType is the action to execute upon the player list. The entries that follow specify which entries are added or removed from the player list. |
| `entries` | `[]protocol.PlayerListEntry` | Entries is a list of all player list entries that should be added/removed from the player list, depending on the ActionType set. |
| `unknown1` | `[]protocol.NeteaseUnknownPlayerListEntry` | Netease |
| `unknown2` | `[]protocol.NeteaseUnknownPlayerListEntry` | Netease |
| `unknown3` | `[]string` | Netease |
| `growth_levels` | `[]uint32` | Netease: launcher levels (1 - 50), such as "Diamond V", "Bedrock III".. |
| `unknown4` | `[]bool` | Netease |

### entries 嵌套字段

- `uuid` (`uuid.UUID`)：UUID is the UUID of the player as sent in the Login packet when the client joined the server. It must match this UUID exactly for the correct XBOX Live icon to show up in the list.
- `entity_unique_id` (`int64`)：EntityUniqueID is the unique entity ID of the player. This ID typically stays consistent during the lifetime of a world, but servers often send the runtime ID for this.
- `username` (`string`)：Username is the username that is shown in the player list of the player that obtains a PlayerList packet with this entry. It does not have to be the same as the actual username of the player.
- `xuid` (`string`)：XUID is the XBOX Live user ID of the player, which will remain consistent as long as the player is logged in with the XBOX Live account.
- `platform_chat_id` (`string`)：PlatformChatID is an identifier only set for particular platforms when chatting (presumably only for Nintendo Switch). It is otherwise an empty string, and is used to decide which players are able to chat with each other.
- `build_platform` (`int32`)：BuildPlatform is the platform of the player as sent by that player in the Login packet.
- `skin` (`Skin`)：Skin is the skin of the player that should be added to the player list. Once sent here, it will not have to be sent again.
- `skin.skin_id` (`string`)：SkinID is a unique ID produced for the skin, for example 'c18e65aa-7b21-4637-9b63-8ad63622ef01_Alex' for the default Alex skin.
- `skin.play_fab_id` (`string`)：PlayFabID is the PlayFab ID produced for the skin. PlayFab is the company that hosts the Marketplace, skins and other related features from the game. This ID is the ID of the skin used to store the skin inside of PlayFab.
- `skin.skin_resource_patch` (`[]byte`)：SkinResourcePatch is a JSON encoded object holding some fields that point to the geometry that the skin has. The JSON object that this holds specifies the way that the geometry of animations and the default skin of the player are combined.
- `skin.skin_data` (`[]byte`)：SkinData is a byte slice of SkinImageWidth * SkinImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte representation of the skin pixels.
- `skin.animations` (`[]SkinAnimation`)：Animations is a list of all animations that the skin has.
- `skin.animations.image_data` (`[]byte`)：ImageData is a byte slice of ImageWidth * ImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte representation of the animation image pixels. The ImageData contains FrameCount images in it, which each represent one stage of the animation. The actual part of the skin that this field holds depends on the AnimationType, where SkinAnimationHead holds only the head and its hat, whereas the other animations hold the entire body of the skin.
- `skin.animations.animation_type` (`uint32`)：AnimationType is the type of the animation, which is one of the types found above. The data that ImageData contains depends on this type.
- `skin.animations.frame_count` (`float32`)：FrameCount is the amount of frames that the skin animation holds. The number of frames here is the amount of images that may be found in the ImageData field.
- `skin.animations.expression_type` (`uint32`)：ExpressionType is the type of expression made by the skin, which is one the types found above.
- `skin.cape_data` (`[]byte`)：CapeData is a byte slice of 64*32*4 bytes. It is a RGBA ordered byte representation of the cape colours, much like the SkinData.
- `skin.skin_geometry` (`[]byte`)：SkinGeometry is a JSON encoded structure of the geometry data of a skin, containing properties such as bones, uv, pivot etc.
- `skin.animation_data` (`[]byte`)：TODO: Find out what value AnimationData holds and when it does hold something.
- `skin.geometry_data_engine_version` (`[]byte`)：GeometryDataEngineVersion ...
- `skin.premium_skin` (`bool`)：PremiumSkin specifies if this is a skin that was purchased from the marketplace.
- `skin.persona_skin` (`bool`)：PersonaSkin specifies if this is a skin that was created using the in-game skin creator.
- `skin.persona_cape_on_classic_skin` (`bool`)：PersonaCapeOnClassicSkin specifies if the skin had a Persona cape (in-game skin creator cape) equipped on a classic skin.
- `skin.primary_user` (`bool`)：PrimaryUser ...
- `skin.cape_id` (`string`)：CapeID is a unique identifier that identifies the cape. It usually holds a UUID in it.
- `skin.full_id` (`string`)：FullID is an ID that represents the skin in full. The actual functionality is unknown: The client does not seem to send a value for this.
- `skin.skin_colour` (`string`)：SkinColour is a hex representation (including #) of the base colour of the skin. An example of the colour sent here is '#b37b62'.
- `skin.arm_size` (`string`)：ArmSize is the size of the arms of the player's model. This is either 'wide' (generally for male skins) or 'slim' (generally for female skins).
- `skin.persona_pieces` (`[]PersonaPiece`)：PersonaPieces is a list of all persona pieces that the skin is composed of.
- `skin.persona_pieces.piece_id` (`string`)：PieceId is a UUID that identifies the piece itself, which is unique for each separate piece.
- `skin.persona_pieces.piece_type` (`string`)：PieceType holds the type of the piece. Several types I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_skeleton - persona_body - persona_skin - persona_bottom - persona_feet - persona_top - persona_mouth - persona_hair - persona_eyes - persona_facial_hair
- `skin.persona_pieces.pack_id` (`string`)：PackID is a UUID that identifies the pack that the persona piece belongs to.
- `skin.persona_pieces.default` (`bool`)：Default specifies if the piece is one of the default pieces. This is true when the piece is one of those that a Steve or Alex skin have.
- `skin.persona_pieces.product_id` (`string`)：ProductID is a UUID that identifies the piece when it comes to purchases. It is empty for pieces that have the 'Default' field set to true.
- `skin.piece_tint_colours` (`[]PersonaPieceTintColour`)：PieceTintColours is a list of specific tint colours for (some of) the persona pieces found in the list above.
- `skin.piece_tint_colours.piece_type` (`string`)：PieceType is the type of the persona skin piece that this tint colour concerns. The piece type must always be present in the persona pieces list, but not each piece type has a tint colour sent. Pieces that do have a tint colour that I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_mouth - persona_eyes - persona_hair
- `skin.piece_tint_colours.colours` (`[]string`)：Colours is a list four colours written in hex notation (note, that unlike the SkinColour field in the ClientData struct, this is actually ARGB, not just RGB). The colours refer to different parts of the skin piece. The 'persona_eyes' may have the following colours: ["#ffa12722","#ff2f1f0f","#ff3aafd9","#0"] The first hex colour represents the tint colour of the iris, the second hex colour represents the eyebrows and the third represents the sclera. The fourth is #0 because there are only 3 parts of the persona_eyes skin piece.
- `skin.trusted` (`bool`)：Trusted specifies if the skin is 'trusted'. No code should rely on this field, as any proxy or client can easily change it.
- `skin.override_appearance` (`bool`)：OverrideAppearance specifies if the skin should override the player's skin that is equipped client-side. When false, the client will reject the skin and continue to use the skin that the player has equipped.
- `teacher` (`bool`)：Teacher is a Minecraft: Education Edition field. It specifies if the player to be added to the player list is a teacher.
- `host` (`bool`)：Host specifies if the player that is added to the player list is the host of the game.
- `sub_client` (`bool`)：SubClient specifies if the player that is added to the player list is a sub-client of another player.
- `player_colour` (`color.RGBA`)：PlayerColour is the colour of the player that is shown in UI elements, currently only used for the player locator bar.

fields.name: map_id
fields.note: MapID is the unique identifier that represents the map that is updated over network. It remains consistent across sessions.

fields.name: update_flags
fields.note: UpdateFlags is a combination of flags found above that indicate what parts of the map should be updated client-side.

fields.name: dimension
fields.note: Dimension is the dimension of the map that should be updated, for example the overworld (0), the nether (1) or the end (2).

fields.name: locked_map
fields.note: LockedMap specifies if the map that was updated was a locked map, which may be done using a cartography table.

fields.name: origin
fields.note: Origin is the center position of the map being updated.

fields.name: scale
fields.note: Scale is the scale of the map as it is shown in-game. It is written when any of the MapUpdateFlags are set to the UpdateFlags field.

fields.name: maps_included_in
fields.note: The following fields apply only for the MapUpdateFlagInitialisation. MapsIncludedIn holds an array of map IDs that the map updated is included in. This has to do with the scale of the map: Each map holds its own map ID and all map IDs of maps that include this map and have a bigger scale. This means that a scale 0 map will have 5 map IDs in this slice, whereas a scale 4 map will have only 1 (its own). The actual use of this field remains unknown.

fields.name: tracked_objects
fields.note: The following fields apply only for the MapUpdateFlagDecoration. TrackedObjects is a list of tracked objects on the map, which may either be entities or blocks. The client makes sure these tracked objects are actually tracked. (position updated etc.)

children.name: type
children.note: Type is the type of the tracked object. It is either MapObjectTypeEntity or MapObjectTypeBlock.

children.name: entity_unique_id
children.note: EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity, if the tracked object was an entity. It needs not to be filled out if Type is not MapObjectTypeEntity.

children.name: block_position
children.note: BlockPosition is the position of the block, if the tracked object was a block. It needs not to be filled out if Type is not MapObjectTypeBlock.

fields.name: decorations
fields.note: Decorations is a list of fixed decorations located on the map. The decorations will not change client-side, unless the server updates them.

children.name: type
children.note: Type is the type of the map decoration. The type specifies the shape (and sometimes the colour) that the map decoration gets. It is one of the MapDecorationType constants above.

children.name: rotation
children.note: Rotation is the rotation of the map decoration. It is byte due to the 16 fixed directions that the map decoration may face.

children.name: x
children.note: X is the offset on the X axis in pixels of the decoration.

children.name: y
children.note: Y is the offset on the Y axis in pixels of the decoration.

children.name: label
children.note: Label is the name of the map decoration. This name may be of any value.

children.name: colour
children.note: Colour is the colour of the map decoration. Some map decoration types have a specific colour set automatically, whereas others may be changed.

fields.name: height
fields.note: The following fields apply only for the MapUpdateFlagTexture update flag. Height is the height of the texture area that was updated. The height may be a subset of the total height of the map.

fields.name: width
fields.note: Width is the width of the texture area that was updated. The width may be a subset of the total width of the map.

fields.name: xoffset
fields.note: XOffset is the X offset in pixels at which the updated texture area starts. From this X, the updated texture will extend exactly Width pixels to the right.

fields.name: yoffset
fields.note: YOffset is the Y offset in pixels at which the updated texture area starts. From this Y, the updated texture will extend exactly Height pixels up.

fields.name: pixels
fields.note: Pixels is a list of pixel colours for the new texture of the map. It is indexed as Pixels[y*height + x].

It is sent with a combination of flags that specify what data is updated. The ClientBoundMapItemData packet may be used to update specific parts of the map only. It is not required to send the entire map each time when updating one part.

## 67 · ClientBoundMapItemData · 客户端定向地图物品数据

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
- 本内核原始说明：ClientBoundMapItemData is sent by the server to the client to update the data of a map shown to the client. It is sent with a combination of flags that specify what data is updated. The ClientBoundMapItemData packet may be used to update specific parts of the map only. It is not required to send the entire map each time when updating one part.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `map_id` | `int64` | MapID is the unique identifier that represents the map that is updated over network. It remains consistent across sessions. |
| `update_flags` | `uint32` | UpdateFlags is a combination of flags found above that indicate what parts of the map should be updated client-side. |
| `dimension` | `uint8` | Dimension is the dimension of the map that should be updated, for example the overworld (0), the nether (1) or the end (2). |
| `locked_map` | `bool` | LockedMap specifies if the map that was updated was a locked map, which may be done using a cartography table. |
| `origin` | `protocol.BlockPos` | Origin is the center position of the map being updated. |
| `scale` | `uint8` | Scale is the scale of the map as it is shown in-game. It is written when any of the MapUpdateFlags are set to the UpdateFlags field. |
| `maps_included_in` | `[]int64` | The following fields apply only for the MapUpdateFlagInitialisation. MapsIncludedIn holds an array of map IDs that the map updated is included in. This has to do with the scale of the map: Each map holds its own map ID and all map IDs of maps that include this map and have a bigger scale. This means that a scale 0 map will have 5 map IDs in this slice, whereas a scale 4 map will have only 1 (its own). The actual use of this field remains unknown. |
| `tracked_objects` | `[]protocol.MapTrackedObject` | The following fields apply only for the MapUpdateFlagDecoration. TrackedObjects is a list of tracked objects on the map, which may either be entities or blocks. The client makes sure these tracked objects are actually tracked. (position updated etc.) |
| `decorations` | `[]protocol.MapDecoration` | Decorations is a list of fixed decorations located on the map. The decorations will not change client-side, unless the server updates them. |
| `height` | `int32` | The following fields apply only for the MapUpdateFlagTexture update flag. Height is the height of the texture area that was updated. The height may be a subset of the total height of the map. |
| `width` | `int32` | Width is the width of the texture area that was updated. The width may be a subset of the total width of the map. |
| `xoffset` | `int32` | XOffset is the X offset in pixels at which the updated texture area starts. From this X, the updated texture will extend exactly Width pixels to the right. |
| `yoffset` | `int32` | YOffset is the Y offset in pixels at which the updated texture area starts. From this Y, the updated texture will extend exactly Height pixels up. |
| `pixels` | `[]color.RGBA` | Pixels is a list of pixel colours for the new texture of the map. It is indexed as Pixels[y*height + x]. |

### tracked_objects 嵌套字段

- `type` (`int32`)：Type is the type of the tracked object. It is either MapObjectTypeEntity or MapObjectTypeBlock.
- `entity_unique_id` (`int64`)：EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity, if the tracked object was an entity. It needs not to be filled out if Type is not MapObjectTypeEntity.
- `block_position` (`BlockPos`)：BlockPosition is the position of the block, if the tracked object was a block. It needs not to be filled out if Type is not MapObjectTypeBlock.

### decorations 嵌套字段

- `type` (`byte`)：Type is the type of the map decoration. The type specifies the shape (and sometimes the colour) that the map decoration gets. It is one of the MapDecorationType constants above.
- `rotation` (`byte`)：Rotation is the rotation of the map decoration. It is byte due to the 16 fixed directions that the map decoration may face.
- `x` (`byte`)：X is the offset on the X axis in pixels of the decoration.
- `y` (`byte`)：Y is the offset on the Y axis in pixels of the decoration.
- `label` (`string`)：Label is the name of the map decoration. This name may be of any value.
- `colour` (`color.RGBA`)：Colour is the colour of the map decoration. Some map decoration types have a specific colour set automatically, whereas others may be changed.

## 69 · RequestChunkRadius · 本机请求视距

- 分组：世界与结构
- 方向：客户端→服务器
- 用法与边界：服务器可裁剪范围，应读ChunkRadiusUpdated确认，不能无条件强迫加载全图。

fields.name: game_rules
fields.note: GameRules defines game rules changed with their respective values. The value of these game rules may be either 'bool', 'int32' or 'float32'. Note that some game rules are server side only, and don't necessarily need to be sent to the client. Only changed game rules need to be sent in this packet. Game rules that were not changed do not need to be sent if the client is already updated on them.

children.name: can_be_modified_by_player

fields.name: enum_values
fields.note: EnumValues is a slice of all enum values of any enum in the AvailableCommands packet. EnumValues generally should contain each possible value only once. Enums are built by pointing to entries in this slice.

fields.name: chained_subcommand_values
fields.note: ChainedSubcommandValues is a slice of all chained subcommand names. ChainedSubcommandValues generally should contain each possible value only once. ChainedSubcommands are built by pointing to entries in this slice.

fields.name: suffixes
fields.note: Suffixes, like EnumValues, is a slice of all suffix values of any command parameter in the AvailableCommands packet.

fields.name: enums
fields.note: Enums is a slice of all (fixed) command enums present in any of the commands.

children.name: type
children.note: Type is the type of the command enum. The type will show up in the command usage as the type of the argument if it has a certain amount of arguments, or when Options is set to true in the command holding the enum.

children.name: value_indices
children.note: ValueIndices holds a list of indices that point to the EnumValues slice in the AvailableCommandsPacket. These represent the options of the enum.

fields.name: chained_subcommands
fields.note: ChainedSubcommands is a slice of all subcommands that are followed by a chained command. An example usage of this is /execute which allows you to run another command as another entity or at a different position etc.

children.name: name
children.note: Name is the name of the chained subcommand and shows up in the list as a regular subcommand enum.

children.name: values
children.note: Values contains the index and parameter type of the chained subcommand.

children.name: index
children.note: Index is the index of the argument in the ChainedSubcommandValues slice from the AvailableCommands packet. This is then used to set the type specified by the Value field below.

children.name: value
children.note: Value is a combination of the flags above and specified the type of argument. Unlike regular parameter types, this should NOT contain any of the special flags (valid, enum, suffixed or soft enum) but only the basic types.

fields.name: commands
fields.note: Commands is a list of all commands that the client should show client-side. The AvailableCommands packet replaces any commands sent before. It does not only add the commands that are sent in it.

children.name: name
children.note: Name is the name of the command. The command may be executed using this name, and will be shown in the /help list with it. It currently seems that the client crashes if the Name contains uppercase letters.

children.name: description
children.note: Description is the description of the command. It is shown in the /help list and when starting to write a command.

children.name: flags
children.note: Flags is a combination of flags not currently known. Leaving the Flags field empty appears to work.

children.name: permission_level
children.note: PermissionLevel is the command permission level that the player required to execute this command. The field no longer seems to serve a purpose, as the client does not handle the execution of commands anymore: The permissions should be checked server-side.

children.name: aliases_offset
children.note: AliasesOffset is the offset to a CommandEnum that holds the values that should be used as aliases for this command.

children.name: chained_subcommand_offsets
children.note: ChainedSubcommandOffsets is a slice of offsets that all point to a different ChainedSubcommand from the ChainedSubcommands slice in the AvailableCommands packet.

children.name: overloads
children.note: Overloads is a list of command overloads that specify the ways in which a command may be executed. The overloads may be completely different.

children.name: chaining
children.note: Chaining determines if the parameters use chained subcommands or not.

children.name: parameters
children.note: Parameters is a list of command parameters that are part of the overload. These parameters specify the usage of the command when this overload is applied.

children.name: name
children.note: Name is the name of the command parameter. It shows up in the usage like <$Name: $Type>, with the exception of enum types, which show up simply as a list of options if the list is short enough and Options is set to false.

children.name: type
children.note: Type is a rather odd combination of type(flag)s that result in a certain parameter type to show up client-side. It is a combination of the flags above. The basic types must be combined with the ArgumentTypeFlagBasic flag (and integers with a suffix ArgumentTypeFlagSuffixed), whereas enums are combined with the ArgumentTypeFlagEnum flag.

children.name: optional
children.note: Optional specifies if the command parameter is optional to enter. Note that no non-optional parameter should ever be present in a command overload after an optional parameter. When optional, the parameter shows up like so: [$Name: $Type], whereas when mandatory, it shows up like so: <$Name: $Type>.

children.name: options
children.note: Options holds a combinations of options that additionally apply to the command parameter. The list of options can be found above.

fields.name: dynamic_enums
fields.note: DynamicEnums is a slice of dynamic command enums. These command enums can be changed during runtime without having to resend an AvailableCommands packet.

children.name: type
children.note: Type is the type of the command enum. The type will show up in the command usage as the type of the argument if it has a certain amount of arguments, or when Options is set to true in the command holding the enum.

children.name: values
children.note: Values is a slice of possible options for the enum.

fields.name: constraints
fields.note: Constraints is a list of constraints that should be applied to certain options of enums in the commands above.

children.name: enum_value_index
children.note: EnumValueIndex points to an enum value in the AvailableCommands packet that this constraint should apply to.

children.name: enum_index
children.note: EnumIndex points to an enum in the AvailableCommands packet to which this constraint should apply to.

children.name: constraints
children.note: Constraints holds a slice of constraints as present in the constants above.

packets.name: AvailableCommands
packets.title: 服务器可用命令与参数
packets.usage: 命令名、描述、权限、重载、枚举等；适合AI查询真实服务器支持的命令，不代表可提升权限。
packets.description: AvailableCommands is sent by the server to send a list of all commands that the player is able to use on the server. This packet holds all the arguments of each commands as well, making it possible for the client to provide auto-completion and command usages. AvailableCommands packets can be resent, but the packet is often very big, so doing this very often should be avoided.
packets.content:
## 76 · AvailableCommands · 服务器可用命令与参数

- 分组：命令与计分板
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：命令名、描述、权限、重载、枚举等；适合AI查询真实服务器支持的命令，不代表可提升权限。
- 本内核原始说明：AvailableCommands is sent by the server to send a list of all commands that the player is able to use on the server. This packet holds all the arguments of each commands as well, making it possible for the client to provide auto-completion and command usages. AvailableCommands packets can be resent, but the packet is often very big, so doing this very often should be avoided.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `enum_values` | `[]string` | EnumValues is a slice of all enum values of any enum in the AvailableCommands packet. EnumValues generally should contain each possible value only once. Enums are built by pointing to entries in this slice. |
| `chained_subcommand_values` | `[]string` | ChainedSubcommandValues is a slice of all chained subcommand names. ChainedSubcommandValues generally should contain each possible value only once. ChainedSubcommands are built by pointing to entries in this slice. |
| `suffixes` | `[]string` | Suffixes, like EnumValues, is a slice of all suffix values of any command parameter in the AvailableCommands packet. |
| `enums` | `[]protocol.CommandEnum` | Enums is a slice of all (fixed) command enums present in any of the commands. |
| `chained_subcommands` | `[]protocol.ChainedSubcommand` | ChainedSubcommands is a slice of all subcommands that are followed by a chained command. An example usage of this is /execute which allows you to run another command as another entity or at a different position etc. |
| `commands` | `[]protocol.Command` | Commands is a list of all commands that the client should show client-side. The AvailableCommands packet replaces any commands sent before. It does not only add the commands that are sent in it. |
| `dynamic_enums` | `[]protocol.DynamicEnum` | DynamicEnums is a slice of dynamic command enums. These command enums can be changed during runtime without having to resend an AvailableCommands packet. |
| `constraints` | `[]protocol.CommandEnumConstraint` | Constraints is a list of constraints that should be applied to certain options of enums in the commands above. |

### enums 嵌套字段

- `type` (`string`)：Type is the type of the command enum. The type will show up in the command usage as the type of the argument if it has a certain amount of arguments, or when Options is set to true in the command holding the enum.
- `value_indices` (`[]uint`)：ValueIndices holds a list of indices that point to the EnumValues slice in the AvailableCommandsPacket. These represent the options of the enum.

### chained_subcommands 嵌套字段

- `name` (`string`)：Name is the name of the chained subcommand and shows up in the list as a regular subcommand enum.
- `values` (`[]ChainedSubcommandValue`)：Values contains the index and parameter type of the chained subcommand.
- `values.index` (`uint16`)：Index is the index of the argument in the ChainedSubcommandValues slice from the AvailableCommands packet. This is then used to set the type specified by the Value field below.
- `values.value` (`uint16`)：Value is a combination of the flags above and specified the type of argument. Unlike regular parameter types, this should NOT contain any of the special flags (valid, enum, suffixed or soft enum) but only the basic types.

### commands 嵌套字段

- `name` (`string`)：Name is the name of the command. The command may be executed using this name, and will be shown in the /help list with it. It currently seems that the client crashes if the Name contains uppercase letters.
- `description` (`string`)：Description is the description of the command. It is shown in the /help list and when starting to write a command.
- `flags` (`uint16`)：Flags is a combination of flags not currently known. Leaving the Flags field empty appears to work.
- `permission_level` (`byte`)：PermissionLevel is the command permission level that the player required to execute this command. The field no longer seems to serve a purpose, as the client does not handle the execution of commands anymore: The permissions should be checked server-side.
- `aliases_offset` (`uint32`)：AliasesOffset is the offset to a CommandEnum that holds the values that should be used as aliases for this command.
- `chained_subcommand_offsets` (`[]uint16`)：ChainedSubcommandOffsets is a slice of offsets that all point to a different ChainedSubcommand from the ChainedSubcommands slice in the AvailableCommands packet.
- `overloads` (`[]CommandOverload`)：Overloads is a list of command overloads that specify the ways in which a command may be executed. The overloads may be completely different.
- `overloads.chaining` (`bool`)：Chaining determines if the parameters use chained subcommands or not.
- `overloads.parameters` (`[]CommandParameter`)：Parameters is a list of command parameters that are part of the overload. These parameters specify the usage of the command when this overload is applied.
- `overloads.parameters.name` (`string`)：Name is the name of the command parameter. It shows up in the usage like <$Name: $Type>, with the exception of enum types, which show up simply as a list of options if the list is short enough and Options is set to false.
- `overloads.parameters.type` (`uint32`)：Type is a rather odd combination of type(flag)s that result in a certain parameter type to show up client-side. It is a combination of the flags above. The basic types must be combined with the ArgumentTypeFlagBasic flag (and integers with a suffix ArgumentTypeFlagSuffixed), whereas enums are combined with the ArgumentTypeFlagEnum flag.
- `overloads.parameters.optional` (`bool`)：Optional specifies if the command parameter is optional to enter. Note that no non-optional parameter should ever be present in a command overload after an optional parameter. When optional, the parameter shows up like so: [$Name: $Type], whereas when mandatory, it shows up like so: <$Name: $Type>.
- `overloads.parameters.options` (`byte`)：Options holds a combinations of options that additionally apply to the command parameter. The list of options can be found above.

### dynamic_enums 嵌套字段

- `type` (`string`)：Type is the type of the command enum. The type will show up in the command usage as the type of the argument if it has a certain amount of arguments, or when Options is set to true in the command holding the enum.
- `values` (`[]string`)：Values is a slice of possible options for the enum.

### constraints 嵌套字段

- `enum_value_index` (`uint32`)：EnumValueIndex points to an enum value in the AvailableCommands packet that this constraint should apply to.
- `enum_index` (`uint32`)：EnumIndex points to an enum in the AvailableCommands packet to which this constraint should apply to.
- `constraints` (`[]byte`)：Constraints holds a slice of constraints as present in the constants above.

fields.name: command_line
fields.note: CommandLine is the raw entered command line. The client does no parsing of the command line by itself (unlike it did in the early stages), but lets the server do that.

fields.name: command_origin
fields.note: CommandOrigin is the data specifying the origin of the command. In other words, the source that the command was from, such as the player itself or a websocket server.

children.name: origin

fields.note: Internal specifies if the command request internal. Setting it to false seems to work and the usage of this field is not known.

packets.title: 命令执行请求
packets.usage: 携带CommandLine和CommandOrigin；确认路径匹配UUID返回CommandOutput。需要实际权限。
packets.description: CommandRequest is sent by the client to request the execution of a server-side command. Although some servers support sending commands using the Text packet, this packet is guaranteed to have the correct result.
packets.content:
## 77 · CommandRequest · 命令执行请求

- 分组：命令与计分板
- 方向：客户端→服务器
- 用法与边界：携带CommandLine和CommandOrigin；确认路径匹配UUID返回CommandOutput。需要实际权限。
- 本内核原始说明：CommandRequest is sent by the client to request the execution of a server-side command. Although some servers support sending commands using the Text packet, this packet is guaranteed to have the correct result.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `command_line` | `string` | CommandLine is the raw entered command line. The client does no parsing of the command line by itself (unlike it did in the early stages), but lets the server do that. |
| `command_origin` | `protocol.CommandOrigin` | CommandOrigin is the data specifying the origin of the command. In other words, the source that the command was from, such as the player itself or a websocket server. |
| `internal` | `bool` | Internal specifies if the command request internal. Setting it to false seems to work and the usage of this field is not known. |
| `version` | `int32` | Version is the version of the command that is being executed. This field currently has no purpose or functionality. |
| `un_limited` | `bool` | PhoenixBuilder specific fields. Author: LNSSPsd  NetEase specified field |

### command_origin 嵌套字段

- `origin` (`uint32`)：Origin is one of the values above that specifies the origin of the command. The origin may change, depending on what part of the client actually called the command. The command may be issued by a websocket server, for example.
- `uuid` (`uuid.UUID`)：UUID is a unique identifier for every instantiation of a command.
- `request_id` (`string`)：RequestID is an ID that identifies the request of the client. The server should send a CommandOrigin with the same request ID to ensure it can be matched with the request by the caller of the command. This is especially important for websocket servers and it seems that this field is only non-empty for these websocket servers.
- `player_unique_id` (`int64`)：PlayerUniqueID is an ID that identifies the player, the same as the one found in the AdventureSettings packet. Filling it out with 0 seems to work. PlayerUniqueID is only written if Origin is CommandOriginDevConsole or CommandOriginTest.

fields.name: block
fields.note: Block specifies if the command block updated was an actual physical block. If false, the command block is in a minecart and has an entity runtime ID instead.

fields.name: position
fields.note: 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position of the command block updated. It is only set if Block is set to true. Nothing happens if no command block is set at this position.

fields.name: mode
fields.note: Mode is the mode of the command block. It is either CommandBlockImpulse, CommandBlockChain or CommandBlockRepeat. It is only set if Block is set to true.

fields.name: needs_redstone
fields.note: NeedsRedstone specifies if the command block needs to be powered by redstone to be activated. If false, the command block is always active. The field is only set if Block is set to true.

fields.name: conditional
fields.note: Conditional specifies the behaviour of the command block if the command block before it (the opposite side of the direction the arrow if facing) fails to execute. If set to false, it will activate at all times, whereas if set to true, it will activate only if the previous command block executed successfully. The field is only set if Block is set to true.

fields.name: minecart_entity_runtime_id
fields.note: MinecartEntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the minecart entity carrying the command block that is updated. It is set only if Block is set to false.

fields.name: command
fields.note: Command is the command currently entered in the command block. This is the command that is executed when the command block is activated.

fields.name: last_output
fields.note: LastOutput is the output of the last command executed by the command block. It may be left empty to show simply no output at all, in combination with setting ShouldTrackOutput to false.

fields.name: name

packets.content:
## 78 · CommandBlockUpdate · 命令方块更新

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：客户端→服务器
- 用法与边界：用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
- 本内核原始说明：CommandBlockUpdate is sent by the client to update a command block at a specific position. The command block may be either a physical block or an entity.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `block` | `bool` | Block specifies if the command block updated was an actual physical block. If false, the command block is in a minecart and has an entity runtime ID instead. |
| `position` | `protocol.BlockPos` | 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position of the command block updated. It is only set if Block is set to true. Nothing happens if no command block is set at this position. |
| `mode` | `uint32` | Mode is the mode of the command block. It is either CommandBlockImpulse, CommandBlockChain or CommandBlockRepeat. It is only set if Block is set to true. |
| `needs_redstone` | `bool` | NeedsRedstone specifies if the command block needs to be powered by redstone to be activated. If false, the command block is always active. The field is only set if Block is set to true. |
| `conditional` | `bool` | Conditional specifies the behaviour of the command block if the command block before it (the opposite side of the direction the arrow if facing) fails to execute. If set to false, it will activate at all times, whereas if set to true, it will activate only if the previous command block executed successfully. The field is only set if Block is set to true. |
| `minecart_entity_runtime_id` | `uint64` | MinecartEntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the minecart entity carrying the command block that is updated. It is set only if Block is set to false. |
| `command` | `string` | Command is the command currently entered in the command block. This is the command that is executed when the command block is activated. |
| `last_output` | `string` | LastOutput is the output of the last command executed by the command block. It may be left empty to show simply no output at all, in combination with setting ShouldTrackOutput to false. |
| `name` | `string` | Name is the name of the command block updated. If not empty, it will show this name hovering above the command block when hovering over the block with the cursor. |
| `filtered_name` | `string` | FilteredName is a filtered version of Name with all the profanity removed. The client will use this over Name if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled. |
| `should_track_output` | `bool` | ShouldTrackOutput specifies if the command block tracks output. If set to false, the output box won't be shown within the command block. |
| `execute_on_first_tick` | `bool` | ExecuteOnFirstTick specifies if the command block should execute on the first tick, AKA as soon as the command block is enabled. |
| `tick_delay` | `int32` | TickDelay is the delay in ticks between executions of a command block, if it is a repeating command block. |

fields.name: command_origin

children.name: origin

children.name: request_id
children.note: RequestID is an ID that identifies the request of the client. The server should send a CommandOrigin with the same request ID to ensure it can be matched with the request by the caller of the command. This is especially important for websocket servers and it seems that this field is only non-empty for these websocket servers.

children.name: player_unique_id

fields.name: success_count

packets.name: CommandOutput
packets.title: 命令执行结果
packets.usage: SuccessCount/消息参数/DataSet，判断成功与条件分支；超时仍是未知，不能当失败后自动重发副作用。
packets.description: CommandOutput is sent by the server to the client to send text as output of a command. Most servers do not use this packet and instead simply send Text packets, but there is reason to send it. If the origin of a CommandRequest packet is not the player itself, but, for example, a websocket server, sending a Text packet will not do what is expected: The message should go to the websocket server, not to the client's chat. The CommandOutput packet will make sure the messages are relayed to the correct origin of the command request.
packets.content:
## 79 · CommandOutput · 命令执行结果

- 分组：命令与计分板
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：SuccessCount/消息参数/DataSet，判断成功与条件分支；超时仍是未知，不能当失败后自动重发副作用。
- 本内核原始说明：CommandOutput is sent by the server to the client to send text as output of a command. Most servers do not use this packet and instead simply send Text packets, but there is reason to send it. If the origin of a CommandRequest packet is not the player itself, but, for example, a websocket server, sending a Text packet will not do what is expected: The message should go to the websocket server, not to the client's chat. The CommandOutput packet will make sure the messages are relayed to the correct origin of the command request.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `command_origin` | `protocol.CommandOrigin` | CommandOrigin is the data specifying the origin of the command. In other words, the source that the command request was from, such as the player itself or a websocket server. The client forwards the messages in this packet to the right origin, depending on what is sent here. |
| `output_type` | `uint8` | OutputType specifies the type of output that is sent. The OutputType sent by vanilla games appears to be 3, which seems to work. |
| `success_count` | `uint32` | 服务端报告成功的数量。 SuccessCount is the amount of times that a command was executed successfully as a result of the command that was requested. For servers, this is usually a rather meaningless fields, but for vanilla, this is applicable for commands created with Functions. |
| `output_messages` | `[]protocol.CommandOutputMessage` | OutputMessages is a list of all output messages that should be sent to the player. Whether they are shown or not, depends on the type of the messages. |
| `data_set` | `string` | DataSet ... TODO: Find out what this is for. |

### command_origin 嵌套字段

- `origin` (`uint32`)：Origin is one of the values above that specifies the origin of the command. The origin may change, depending on what part of the client actually called the command. The command may be issued by a websocket server, for example.
- `uuid` (`uuid.UUID`)：UUID is a unique identifier for every instantiation of a command.
- `request_id` (`string`)：RequestID is an ID that identifies the request of the client. The server should send a CommandOrigin with the same request ID to ensure it can be matched with the request by the caller of the command. This is especially important for websocket servers and it seems that this field is only non-empty for these websocket servers.
- `player_unique_id` (`int64`)：PlayerUniqueID is an ID that identifies the player, the same as the one found in the AdventureSettings packet. Filling it out with 0 seems to work. PlayerUniqueID is only written if Origin is CommandOriginDevConsole or CommandOriginTest.

### output_messages 嵌套字段

- `success` (`bool`)：Success indicates if the output message was one of a successful command execution. If set to true, the output message is by default coloured white, whereas if set to false, the message is by default coloured red.
- `message` (`string`)：Message is the message that is sent to the client in the chat window. It may either be simply a message or a translated built-in string like 'commands.tp.success.coordinates', combined with specific parameters below.
- `parameters` (`[]string`)：Parameters is a list of parameters that serve to supply the message sent with additional information, such as the position that a player was teleported to or the effect that was applied to an entity. These parameters only apply for the Minecraft built-in command output.

packets.usage: 声音名、坐标、音量与音高；须客户端存在对应声音资源。
packets.description: PlaySound is sent by the server to play a sound to the client. Some of the sounds may only be started using this packet and must be stopped using the StopSound packet.
packets.content:
## 86 · PlaySound · 位置声音播放

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：声音名、坐标、音量与音高；须客户端存在对应声音资源。
- 本内核原始说明：PlaySound is sent by the server to play a sound to the client. Some of the sounds may only be started using this packet and must be stopped using the StopSound packet.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `sound_name` | `string` | SoundName is the name of the sound to play. |
| `position` | `mgl32.Vec3` | 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position at which the sound was played. Some sounds do not depend on a position, which will then ignore it, but most of them will play with the direction based on the position compared to the player's position. |
| `volume` | `float32` | Volume is the relative volume of the sound to play. It will be less loud for the player if it is farther away from the position of the sound. |
| `pitch` | `float32` | 俯仰角。 Pitch is the pitch of the sound to play. Some sounds completely ignore this field, whereas others use it to specify the pitch as the field is intended. |

fields.name: sound_name
fields.note: SoundName is the name of the sound that should be stopped from playing. If no sound with this name is currently active, the packet is ignored.

fields.name: stop_all
fields.note: StopAll specifies if all sounds currently playing to the player should be stopped. If set to true, the SoundName field may be left empty.

fields.name: stop_music_legacy
fields.note: StopMusicLegacy is currently unknown.

fields.name: action_type
fields.note: 动作枚举，具体编号使用本内核定义。 ActionType is the type of the action that should be executed upon the title of a player. It is one of the constants above and specifies the response of the client to the packet.

fields.name: text
fields.note: Text is the text of the title, which has a different meaning depending on the ActionType that the packet has. The text is the text of a title, subtitle or action bar, depending on the type set.

fields.name: fade_in_duration
fields.note: FadeInDuration is the duration that the title takes to fade in on the screen of the player. It is measured in 20ths of a second (AKA in ticks).

fields.name: remain_duration
fields.note: RemainDuration is the duration that the title remains on the screen of the player. It is measured in 20ths of a second (AKA in ticks).

fields.name: fade_out_duration
fields.note: FadeOutDuration is the duration that the title takes to fade out of the screen of the player. It is measured in 20ths of a second (AKA in ticks).

fields.name: xuid
fields.note: XUID is the XBOX Live user ID of the player, which will remain consistent as long as the player is logged in with the XBOX Live account. It is empty if the user is not logged into its XBL account.

fields.name: platform_online_id
fields.note: PlatformOnlineID is either a uint64 or an empty string.

fields.name: filtered_message
fields.note: FilteredMessage is a filtered version of Message with all the profanity removed. The client will use this over Message if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

## 88 · SetTitle · 标题与动作栏

- 本内核原始说明：SetTitle is sent by the server to make a title, subtitle or action bar shown to a player. It has several fields that allow setting the duration of the titles.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `action_type` | `int32` | 动作枚举，具体编号使用本内核定义。 ActionType is the type of the action that should be executed upon the title of a player. It is one of the constants above and specifies the response of the client to the packet. |
| `text` | `string` | Text is the text of the title, which has a different meaning depending on the ActionType that the packet has. The text is the text of a title, subtitle or action bar, depending on the type set. |
| `fade_in_duration` | `int32` | FadeInDuration is the duration that the title takes to fade in on the screen of the player. It is measured in 20ths of a second (AKA in ticks). |
| `remain_duration` | `int32` | RemainDuration is the duration that the title remains on the screen of the player. It is measured in 20ths of a second (AKA in ticks). |

fields.name: position
fields.note: 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position of the structure block that is updated.

fields.name: structure_name
fields.note: StructureName is the name of the structure that was set in the structure block's UI. This is the name used to export the structure to a file.

fields.name: filtered_structure_name
fields.note: FilteredStructureName is a filtered version of StructureName with all the profanity removed. The client will use this over StructureName if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

fields.name: data_field
fields.note: DataField is the name of a function to run, usually used during natural generation. A description can be found here: https://minecraft.wiki/w/Structure_Block#Data.

fields.name: include_players
fields.note: IncludePlayers specifies if the 'Include Players' toggle has been enabled, meaning players are also exported by the structure block.

fields.name: show_bounding_box
fields.note: ShowBoundingBox specifies if the structure block should have its bounds outlined. A thin line will encapsulate the bounds of the structure if set to true.

fields.name: structure_block_type
fields.note: StructureBlockType is the type of the structure block updated. A list of structure block types that will be used can be found in the constants above.

fields.name: settings
fields.note: Settings is a struct of settings that should be used for exporting the structure. These settings are identical to the last sent in the StructureBlockUpdate packet by the client.

children.name: palette_name
children.note: PaletteName is the name of the palette used in the structure. Currently, it seems that this field is always 'default'.

children.name: ignore_entities
children.note: IgnoreEntities specifies if the structure should ignore entities or include them. If set to false, entities will also show up in the exported structure.

children.name: ignore_blocks
children.note: IgnoreBlocks specifies if the structure should ignore blocks or include them. If set to false, blocks will show up in the exported structure.

children.name: allow_non_ticking_chunks
children.note: AllowNonTickingChunks specifies if the structure should allow non-ticking chunks. If set to false, the structure will export non-ticking chunks.

children.name: size
children.note: Size is the size of the area that is about to be exported. The area exported will start at the Position + Offset, and will extend as far as Size specifies.

children.name: offset
children.note: Offset is the offset position that was set in the structure block. The area exported is offset by this position.

children.name: last_editing_player_unique_id
children.note: LastEditingPlayerUniqueID is the unique ID of the player that last edited the structure block that these settings concern.

children.name: rotation
children.note: Rotation is the rotation that the structure block should obtain. See the constants above for available options.

children.name: mirror
children.note: Mirror specifies the way the structure should be mirrored. It is either no mirror at all, mirror on the x/z axis or both.

children.name: animation_mode
children.note: AnimationMode ...

children.name: animation_duration
children.note: AnimationDuration ...

children.name: integrity
children.note: Integrity is usually 1, but may be set to a number between 0 and 1 to omit blocks randomly, using the Seed that follows.

children.name: seed
children.note: Seed is the seed used to omit blocks if Integrity is not equal to one. If the Seed is 0, a random seed is selected to omit blocks.

children.name: pivot
children.note: Pivot is the pivot around which the structure may be rotated.

fields.name: redstone_save_mode
fields.note: RedstoneSaveMode is the mode that should be used to save the structure when used with redstone. In Java Edition, this is always stored in memory, but in Bedrock Edition it can be stored either to disk or memory. See the constants above for the options.

fields.name: should_trigger
fields.note: ShouldTrigger specifies if the structure block should be triggered immediately after this packet reaches the server.

fields.name: waterlogged
fields.note: Waterlogged specifies if non-air blocks replace water or combine with water.

packets.name: StructureBlockUpdate
packets.title: 结构方块更新
packets.usage: 用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
packets.description: StructureBlockUpdate is sent by the client when it updates a structure block using the in-game UI. The data it contains depends on the type of structure block that it is. In Minecraft Bedrock Edition v1.11, there is only the Export structure block type, but in v1.13 the ones present in Java Edition will, according to the wiki, be added too.
packets.content:
## 90 · StructureBlockUpdate · 结构方块更新

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：客户端→服务器
- 用法与边界：用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
- 本内核原始说明：StructureBlockUpdate is sent by the client when it updates a structure block using the in-game UI. The data it contains depends on the type of structure block that it is. In Minecraft Bedrock Edition v1.11, there is only the Export structure block type, but in v1.13 the ones present in Java Edition will, according to the wiki, be added too.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `position` | `protocol.BlockPos` | 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position of the structure block that is updated. |
| `structure_name` | `string` | StructureName is the name of the structure that was set in the structure block's UI. This is the name used to export the structure to a file. |
| `filtered_structure_name` | `string` | FilteredStructureName is a filtered version of StructureName with all the profanity removed. The client will use this over StructureName if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled. |
| `data_field` | `string` | DataField is the name of a function to run, usually used during natural generation. A description can be found here: https://minecraft.wiki/w/Structure_Block#Data. |
| `include_players` | `bool` | IncludePlayers specifies if the 'Include Players' toggle has been enabled, meaning players are also exported by the structure block. |
| `show_bounding_box` | `bool` | ShowBoundingBox specifies if the structure block should have its bounds outlined. A thin line will encapsulate the bounds of the structure if set to true. |
| `structure_block_type` | `int32` | StructureBlockType is the type of the structure block updated. A list of structure block types that will be used can be found in the constants above. |
| `settings` | `protocol.StructureSettings` | Settings is a struct of settings that should be used for exporting the structure. These settings are identical to the last sent in the StructureBlockUpdate packet by the client. |
| `redstone_save_mode` | `int32` | RedstoneSaveMode is the mode that should be used to save the structure when used with redstone. In Java Edition, this is always stored in memory, but in Bedrock Edition it can be stored either to disk or memory. See the constants above for the options. |
| `should_trigger` | `bool` | ShouldTrigger specifies if the structure block should be triggered immediately after this packet reaches the server. |
| `waterlogged` | `bool` | Waterlogged specifies if non-air blocks replace water or combine with water. |

### settings 嵌套字段

- `palette_name` (`string`)：PaletteName is the name of the palette used in the structure. Currently, it seems that this field is always 'default'.
- `ignore_entities` (`bool`)：IgnoreEntities specifies if the structure should ignore entities or include them. If set to false, entities will also show up in the exported structure.
- `ignore_blocks` (`bool`)：IgnoreBlocks specifies if the structure should ignore blocks or include them. If set to false, blocks will show up in the exported structure.
- `allow_non_ticking_chunks` (`bool`)：AllowNonTickingChunks specifies if the structure should allow non-ticking chunks. If set to false, the structure will export non-ticking chunks.
- `size` (`BlockPos`)：Size is the size of the area that is about to be exported. The area exported will start at the Position + Offset, and will extend as far as Size specifies.
- `offset` (`BlockPos`)：Offset is the offset position that was set in the structure block. The area exported is offset by this position.
- `last_editing_player_unique_id` (`int64`)：LastEditingPlayerUniqueID is the unique ID of the player that last edited the structure block that these settings concern.
- `rotation` (`byte`)：Rotation is the rotation that the structure block should obtain. See the constants above for available options.
- `mirror` (`byte`)：Mirror specifies the way the structure should be mirrored. It is either no mirror at all, mirror on the x/z axis or both.
- `animation_mode` (`byte`)：AnimationMode ...
- `animation_duration` (`float32`)：AnimationDuration ...
- `integrity` (`float32`)：Integrity is usually 1, but may be set to a number between 0 and 1 to omit blocks randomly, using the Seed that follows.
- `seed` (`uint32`)：Seed is the seed used to omit blocks if Integrity is not equal to one. If the Seed is 0, a random seed is selected to omit blocks.
- `pivot` (`mgl32.Vec3`)：Pivot is the pivot around which the structure may be rotated.

fields.name: offer_id
fields.note: OfferID is a string that identifies the offer for which a window should be opened. ID should be in the format of a UUID, however it can be left empty if StoreOfferTypeServerPage is used.

packets.name: ShowStoreOffer
packets.title: 商店商品显示
packets.usage: 打开商店商品界面；不属于机器人游戏命令执行。
packets.description: ShowStoreOffer is sent by the server to show a Marketplace store offer to a player. It opens a window client-side that displays the item. The ShowStoreOffer packet only works on the partnered servers: Servers that are not partnered will not have a store buttons show up in the in-game pause menu and will, as a result, not be able to open store offers on the client side. Sending the packet does therefore not work when using a proxy that is not connected to with the domain of one of the partnered servers.
packets.content:
## 91 · ShowStoreOffer · 商店商品显示

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：打开商店商品界面；不属于机器人游戏命令执行。

The ShowStoreOffer packet only works on the partnered servers: Servers that are not partnered will not have a store buttons show up in the in-game pause menu and will, as a result, not be able to open store offers on the client side. Sending the packet does therefore not work when using a proxy that is not connected to with the domain of one of the partnered servers.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |

| `type` | `uint8` | Type is the type of the store offer that is being shown to the player. It is one of the constants that may be found above. |

fields.name: uuid
fields.note: UUID is the UUID of the player as sent in the Login packet when the client joined the server. It must match this UUID exactly for the skin to show up on the player.

fields.name: skin
fields.note: Skin is the new skin to be applied on the player with the UUID in the field above. The skin, including its animations, will be shown after sending it.

children.name: skin_id
children.note: SkinID is a unique ID produced for the skin, for example 'c18e65aa-7b21-4637-9b63-8ad63622ef01_Alex' for the default Alex skin.

children.name: play_fab_id
children.note: PlayFabID is the PlayFab ID produced for the skin. PlayFab is the company that hosts the Marketplace, skins and other related features from the game. This ID is the ID of the skin used to store the skin inside of PlayFab.

children.name: skin_resource_patch
children.note: SkinResourcePatch is a JSON encoded object holding some fields that point to the geometry that the skin has. The JSON object that this holds specifies the way that the geometry of animations and the default skin of the player are combined.

children.name: skin_data
children.note: SkinData is a byte slice of SkinImageWidth * SkinImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte representation of the skin pixels.

children.name: animations
children.note: Animations is a list of all animations that the skin has.

children.name: image_data
children.note: ImageData is a byte slice of ImageWidth * ImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte representation of the animation image pixels. The ImageData contains FrameCount images in it, which each represent one stage of the animation. The actual part of the skin that this field holds depends on the AnimationType, where SkinAnimationHead holds only the head and its hat, whereas the other animations hold the entire body of the skin.

children.name: animation_type
children.note: AnimationType is the type of the animation, which is one of the types found above. The data that ImageData contains depends on this type.

children.name: frame_count
children.note: FrameCount is the amount of frames that the skin animation holds. The number of frames here is the amount of images that may be found in the ImageData field.

children.name: expression_type
children.note: ExpressionType is the type of expression made by the skin, which is one the types found above.

children.name: cape_data
children.note: CapeData is a byte slice of 64*32*4 bytes. It is a RGBA ordered byte representation of the cape colours, much like the SkinData.

children.name: skin_geometry
children.note: SkinGeometry is a JSON encoded structure of the geometry data of a skin, containing properties such as bones, uv, pivot etc.

children.name: animation_data
children.note: TODO: Find out what value AnimationData holds and when it does hold something.

children.name: geometry_data_engine_version
children.note: GeometryDataEngineVersion ...

children.name: premium_skin
children.note: PremiumSkin specifies if this is a skin that was purchased from the marketplace.

children.name: persona_skin
children.note: PersonaSkin specifies if this is a skin that was created using the in-game skin creator.

children.name: persona_cape_on_classic_skin
children.note: PersonaCapeOnClassicSkin specifies if the skin had a Persona cape (in-game skin creator cape) equipped on a classic skin.

children.name: primary_user
children.note: PrimaryUser ...

children.name: cape_id
children.note: CapeID is a unique identifier that identifies the cape. It usually holds a UUID in it.

children.name: full_id
children.note: FullID is an ID that represents the skin in full. The actual functionality is unknown: The client does not seem to send a value for this.

children.name: skin_colour
children.note: SkinColour is a hex representation (including #) of the base colour of the skin. An example of the colour sent here is '#b37b62'.

children.name: arm_size
children.note: ArmSize is the size of the arms of the player's model. This is either 'wide' (generally for male skins) or 'slim' (generally for female skins).

children.name: persona_pieces
children.note: PersonaPieces is a list of all persona pieces that the skin is composed of.

children.name: piece_id
children.note: PieceId is a UUID that identifies the piece itself, which is unique for each separate piece.

children.name: piece_type
children.note: PieceType holds the type of the piece. Several types I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_skeleton - persona_body - persona_skin - persona_bottom - persona_feet - persona_top - persona_mouth - persona_hair - persona_eyes - persona_facial_hair

children.name: pack_id
children.note: PackID is a UUID that identifies the pack that the persona piece belongs to.

children.name: default
children.note: Default specifies if the piece is one of the default pieces. This is true when the piece is one of those that a Steve or Alex skin have.

children.name: product_id
children.note: ProductID is a UUID that identifies the piece when it comes to purchases. It is empty for pieces that have the 'Default' field set to true.

children.name: piece_tint_colours
children.note: PieceTintColours is a list of specific tint colours for (some of) the persona pieces found in the list above.

children.name: piece_type
children.note: PieceType is the type of the persona skin piece that this tint colour concerns. The piece type must always be present in the persona pieces list, but not each piece type has a tint colour sent. Pieces that do have a tint colour that I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_mouth - persona_eyes - persona_hair

children.name: colours
children.note: Colours is a list four colours written in hex notation (note, that unlike the SkinColour field in the ClientData struct, this is actually ARGB, not just RGB). The colours refer to different parts of the skin piece. The 'persona_eyes' may have the following colours: ["#ffa12722","#ff2f1f0f","#ff3aafd9","#0"] The first hex colour represents the tint colour of the iris, the second hex colour represents the eyebrows and the third represents the sclera. The fourth is #0 because there are only 3 parts of the persona_eyes skin piece.

children.name: trusted
children.note: Trusted specifies if the skin is 'trusted'. No code should rely on this field, as any proxy or client can easily change it.

children.name: override_appearance
children.note: OverrideAppearance specifies if the skin should override the player's skin that is equipped client-side. When false, the client will reject the skin and continue to use the skin that the player has equipped.

fields.name: new_skin_name
fields.note: NewSkinName no longer has a function: The field can be left empty at all times.

fields.name: old_skin_name
fields.note: OldSkinName no longer has a function: The field can be left empty at all times.
