It is relayed by the server, or sent if the server changes the skin of a player on its own accord. Note that the packet can only be sent for players that are in the player list at the time of sending.
packets.content:
## 93 · PlayerSkin · 玩家皮肤

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：客户端→服务器
- 用法与边界：用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
- 本内核原始说明：PlayerSkin is sent by the client to the server when it updates its own skin using the in-game skin picker. It is relayed by the server, or sent if the server changes the skin of a player on its own accord. Note that the packet can only be sent for players that are in the player list at the time of sending.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `uuid` | `uuid.UUID` | UUID is the UUID of the player as sent in the Login packet when the client joined the server. It must match this UUID exactly for the skin to show up on the player. |
| `skin` | `protocol.Skin` | Skin is the new skin to be applied on the player with the UUID in the field above. The skin, including its animations, will be shown after sending it. |
| `new_skin_name` | `string` | NewSkinName no longer has a function: The field can be left empty at all times. |
| `old_skin_name` | `string` | OldSkinName no longer has a function: The field can be left empty at all times. |

### skin 嵌套字段

- `skin_id` (`string`)：SkinID is a unique ID produced for the skin, for example 'c18e65aa-7b21-4637-9b63-8ad63622ef01_Alex' for the default Alex skin.
- `play_fab_id` (`string`)：PlayFabID is the PlayFab ID produced for the skin. PlayFab is the company that hosts the Marketplace, skins and other related features from the game. This ID is the ID of the skin used to store the skin inside of PlayFab.
- `skin_resource_patch` (`[]byte`)：SkinResourcePatch is a JSON encoded object holding some fields that point to the geometry that the skin has. The JSON object that this holds specifies the way that the geometry of animations and the default skin of the player are combined.
- `skin_data` (`[]byte`)：SkinData is a byte slice of SkinImageWidth * SkinImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte representation of the skin pixels.
- `animations` (`[]SkinAnimation`)：Animations is a list of all animations that the skin has.
- `animations.image_data` (`[]byte`)：ImageData is a byte slice of ImageWidth * ImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte representation of the animation image pixels. The ImageData contains FrameCount images in it, which each represent one stage of the animation. The actual part of the skin that this field holds depends on the AnimationType, where SkinAnimationHead holds only the head and its hat, whereas the other animations hold the entire body of the skin.
- `animations.animation_type` (`uint32`)：AnimationType is the type of the animation, which is one of the types found above. The data that ImageData contains depends on this type.
- `animations.frame_count` (`float32`)：FrameCount is the amount of frames that the skin animation holds. The number of frames here is the amount of images that may be found in the ImageData field.
- `animations.expression_type` (`uint32`)：ExpressionType is the type of expression made by the skin, which is one the types found above.
- `cape_data` (`[]byte`)：CapeData is a byte slice of 64*32*4 bytes. It is a RGBA ordered byte representation of the cape colours, much like the SkinData.
- `skin_geometry` (`[]byte`)：SkinGeometry is a JSON encoded structure of the geometry data of a skin, containing properties such as bones, uv, pivot etc.
- `animation_data` (`[]byte`)：TODO: Find out what value AnimationData holds and when it does hold something.
- `geometry_data_engine_version` (`[]byte`)：GeometryDataEngineVersion ...
- `premium_skin` (`bool`)：PremiumSkin specifies if this is a skin that was purchased from the marketplace.
- `persona_skin` (`bool`)：PersonaSkin specifies if this is a skin that was created using the in-game skin creator.
- `persona_cape_on_classic_skin` (`bool`)：PersonaCapeOnClassicSkin specifies if the skin had a Persona cape (in-game skin creator cape) equipped on a classic skin.
- `primary_user` (`bool`)：PrimaryUser ...
- `cape_id` (`string`)：CapeID is a unique identifier that identifies the cape. It usually holds a UUID in it.
- `full_id` (`string`)：FullID is an ID that represents the skin in full. The actual functionality is unknown: The client does not seem to send a value for this.
- `skin_colour` (`string`)：SkinColour is a hex representation (including #) of the base colour of the skin. An example of the colour sent here is '#b37b62'.
- `arm_size` (`string`)：ArmSize is the size of the arms of the player's model. This is either 'wide' (generally for male skins) or 'slim' (generally for female skins).
- `persona_pieces` (`[]PersonaPiece`)：PersonaPieces is a list of all persona pieces that the skin is composed of.
- `persona_pieces.piece_id` (`string`)：PieceId is a UUID that identifies the piece itself, which is unique for each separate piece.
- `persona_pieces.piece_type` (`string`)：PieceType holds the type of the piece. Several types I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_skeleton - persona_body - persona_skin - persona_bottom - persona_feet - persona_top - persona_mouth - persona_hair - persona_eyes - persona_facial_hair
- `persona_pieces.pack_id` (`string`)：PackID is a UUID that identifies the pack that the persona piece belongs to.
- `persona_pieces.default` (`bool`)：Default specifies if the piece is one of the default pieces. This is true when the piece is one of those that a Steve or Alex skin have.
- `persona_pieces.product_id` (`string`)：ProductID is a UUID that identifies the piece when it comes to purchases. It is empty for pieces that have the 'Default' field set to true.
- `piece_tint_colours` (`[]PersonaPieceTintColour`)：PieceTintColours is a list of specific tint colours for (some of) the persona pieces found in the list above.
- `piece_tint_colours.piece_type` (`string`)：PieceType is the type of the persona skin piece that this tint colour concerns. The piece type must always be present in the persona pieces list, but not each piece type has a tint colour sent. Pieces that do have a tint colour that I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_mouth - persona_eyes - persona_hair
- `piece_tint_colours.colours` (`[]string`)：Colours is a list four colours written in hex notation (note, that unlike the SkinColour field in the ClientData struct, this is actually ARGB, not just RGB). The colours refer to different parts of the skin piece. The 'persona_eyes' may have the following colours: ["#ffa12722","#ff2f1f0f","#ff3aafd9","#0"] The first hex colour represents the tint colour of the iris, the second hex colour represents the eyebrows and the third represents the sclera. The fourth is #0 because there are only 3 parts of the persona_eyes skin piece.
- `trusted` (`bool`)：Trusted specifies if the skin is 'trusted'. No code should rely on this field, as any proxy or client can easily change it.
- `override_appearance` (`bool`)：OverrideAppearance specifies if the skin should override the player's skin that is equipped client-side. When false, the client will reject the skin and continue to use the skin that the player has equipped.

fields.name: action_type
fields.note: 动作枚举，具体编号使用本内核定义。 ActionType is the type of the book edit action. The data obtained depends on what type this is. The action type is one of the constants above.

fields.name: inventory_slot
fields.note: InventorySlot is the slot in which the book that was edited may be found. Typically, the server should check if this slot matches the held item slot of the player.

fields.name: page_number
fields.note: PageNumber is the number of the page that the book edit action concerns. It applies for all actions but the BookActionSign. In BookActionSwapPages, it is one of the pages that was swapped.

fields.name: secondary_page_number
fields.note: SecondaryPageNumber is the page number of the second page that the action concerned. It is only set for the BookActionSwapPages action, in which case it is the other page that is swapped.

fields.name: text
fields.note: Text is the text that was written in a particular page of the book. It applies for the BookActionAddPage and BookActionReplacePage only.

fields.name: photo_name
fields.note: PhotoName is the name of the photo on the page in the book. It applies for the BookActionAddPage and BookActionReplacePage only. Unfortunately, the functionality of this field was removed from the default Minecraft Bedrock Edition. It is still available on Education Edition.

fields.name: title
fields.note: Title is the title that the player has given the book. It applies only for the BookActionSign action.

fields.name: author
fields.note: Author is the author that the player has given the book. It applies only for the BookActionSign action. Note that the author may be freely changed, so no assumptions can be made on if the author is actually the name of a player.

fields.name: xuid
fields.note: XUID is the XBOX Live User ID of the player that edited the book. The field is rather pointless, as the server is already aware of the XUID of the player anyway.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `display_slot` | `string` | DisplaySlot is the slot in which the scoreboard should be displayed. Available options can be found in the constants above. |
| `objective_name` | `string` | ObjectiveName is the name of the objective that the scoreboard displays. Filling out a random unique value for this field works: It is not displayed in the scoreboard. |
| `display_name` | `string` | DisplayName is the name, or title, that is displayed at the top of the scoreboard. |
| `criteria_name` | `string` | CriteriaName is the name of the criteria that need to be fulfilled in order for the score to be increased. This can be any kind of string and does not show up client-side. |
| `sort_order` | `int32` | SortOrder is the order in which entries on the scoreboard should be sorted. It is one of the constants that may be found above. |

fields.name: action_type
fields.note: 动作枚举，具体编号使用本内核定义。 ActionType is the type of the action to execute upon the scoreboard with the entries that the packet has. If ActionType is ScoreboardActionModify, all entries will be added to the scoreboard if not yet present, or modified if already present. If set to ScoreboardActionRemove, all scoreboard entries set will be removed from the scoreboard.

fields.name: entries
fields.note: Entries is a list of all entries that the client should operate on. When modifying, it will add or modify all entries, whereas when removing, it will remove all entries.

children.name: entry_id
children.note: EntryID is a unique identifier of this entry. Each entry that represents a different value should get its own entry ID. When modifying a scoreboard, entries that represent the same line should have the same entry ID.

children.name: objective_name
children.note: ObjectiveName is the name of the objective that this scoreboard entry is for. It must be identical to the one set in the SetDisplayObjective packet previously sent.

children.name: score
children.note: Score is the score that the entry represents. Scoreboard entries are ordered using this score, so in order to get the scoreboard to be ordered as expected when trying to write non-score related text on a scoreboard, this score should be incremented for each entry.

children.name: identity_type
children.note: IdentityType is the identity type of the scoreboard entry. The entry may represent an entity, player or a fake player, as the constants above indicate. In order to write plain text to the scoreboard, ScoreboardIdentityFakePlayer should always be used, in combination with the DisplayName field. A different identity type will use the name of the entity.

children.name: entity_unique_id
children.note: EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of either the player or the entity represented by the scoreboard entry. This field is only used if IdentityType is either ScoreboardIdentityEntity or ScoreboardIdentityPlayer.

children.name: display_name
children.note: DisplayName is the custom name of the scoreboard entry. This field is only used if IdentityType is ScoreboardIdentityFakePlayer. If this identity type is not used, the name of the entity/player will be shown instead.

packets.title: 计分板分数变化

packets.description: SetScore is sent by the server to send the contents of a scoreboard to the player. It may be used to either add, remove or edit entries on the scoreboard.
packets.content:
## 108 · SetScore · 计分板分数变化

- 分组：命令与计分板
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：服务器选择同步的记分板分数；显示板外的全部分数仍可能需OP命令查询。
- 本内核原始说明：SetScore is sent by the server to send the contents of a scoreboard to the player. It may be used to either add, remove or edit entries on the scoreboard.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `action_type` | `uint8` | 动作枚举，具体编号使用本内核定义。 ActionType is the type of the action to execute upon the scoreboard with the entries that the packet has. If ActionType is ScoreboardActionModify, all entries will be added to the scoreboard if not yet present, or modified if already present. If set to ScoreboardActionRemove, all scoreboard entries set will be removed from the scoreboard. |
| `entries` | `[]protocol.ScoreboardEntry` | Entries is a list of all entries that the client should operate on. When modifying, it will add or modify all entries, whereas when removing, it will remove all entries. |

### entries 嵌套字段

- `entry_id` (`int64`)：EntryID is a unique identifier of this entry. Each entry that represents a different value should get its own entry ID. When modifying a scoreboard, entries that represent the same line should have the same entry ID.
- `objective_name` (`string`)：ObjectiveName is the name of the objective that this scoreboard entry is for. It must be identical to the one set in the SetDisplayObjective packet previously sent.
- `score` (`int32`)：Score is the score that the entry represents. Scoreboard entries are ordered using this score, so in order to get the scoreboard to be ordered as expected when trying to write non-score related text on a scoreboard, this score should be incremented for each entry.
- `identity_type` (`byte`)：IdentityType is the identity type of the scoreboard entry. The entry may represent an entity, player or a fake player, as the constants above indicate. In order to write plain text to the scoreboard, ScoreboardIdentityFakePlayer should always be used, in combination with the DisplayName field. A different identity type will use the name of the entity.
- `entity_unique_id` (`int64`)：EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of either the player or the entity represented by the scoreboard entry. This field is only used if IdentityType is either ScoreboardIdentityEntity or ScoreboardIdentityPlayer.
- `display_name` (`string`)：DisplayName is the custom name of the scoreboard entry. This field is only used if IdentityType is ScoreboardIdentityFakePlayer. If this identity type is not used, the name of the entity/player will be shown instead.

fields.name: position
fields.note: 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the block position at which a block is updated.

fields.name: new_block_runtime_id
fields.note: NewBlockRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the block that is placed at Position after sending the packet to the client.

fields.name: flags
fields.note: Flags is a combination of flags that specify the way the block is updated client-side. It is a combination of the flags above, but typically sending only the BlockUpdateNetwork flag is sufficient.

fields.name: layer
fields.note: Layer is the world layer on which the block is updated. For most blocks, this is the first layer, as that layer is the default layer to place blocks on, but for blocks inside of each other, this differs.

fields.name: entity_unique_id
fields.note: 实体唯一ID，与运行ID不同。 EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the falling block entity that the block transitions to or that the entity transitions from. Note that for both possible values for TransitionType, the EntityUniqueID should point to the falling block entity involved.

fields.name: transition_type
fields.note: TransitionType is the type of the transition that happened. It is either BlockToEntityTransition, when a block placed becomes a falling entity, or EntityToBlockTransition, when a falling entity hits the ground and becomes a solid block again.

packets.name: NetworkChunkPublisherUpdate
packets.title: 区块发布中心更新
packets.usage: 服务器的区块中心、半径与已保存区块信息。
packets.description: NetworkChunkPublisherUpdate is sent by the server to change the point around which chunks are and remain loaded. This is useful for mini-game servers, where only one area is ever loaded, in which case the NetworkChunkPublisherUpdate packet can be sent in the middle of it, so that no chunks ever need to be additionally sent during the course of the game. If the packet is not sent at all, no chunks will be shown to the player, regardless of where they are sent.

fields.name: sound_type
fields.note: SoundType is the type of the sound to play. It is one of the constants above. Some of the sound types require additional data, which is set in the EventData field.

fields.name: position
fields.note: 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position of the sound event. The player will be able to hear the direction of the sound based on what position is sent here.

fields.note: ExtraData is a packed integer that some sound types use to provide extra data. An example of this is the note sound, which is composed of a pitch and an instrument type.

fields.name: entity_type
fields.note: EntityType is the string entity type of the entity that emitted the sound, for example 'minecraft:skeleton'. Some sound types use this entity type for additional data.

fields.name: baby_mob
fields.note: BabyMob specifies if the sound should be that of a baby mob. It is most notably used for parrot imitations, which will change based on if this field is set to true or not.

fields.name: disable_relative_volume
fields.note: DisableRelativeVolume specifies if the sound should be played relatively or not. If set to true, the sound will have full volume, regardless of where the Position is, whereas if set to false, the sound's volume will be based on the distance to Position.

fields.name: entity_unique_id
fields.note: 实体唯一ID，与运行ID不同。 EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of a source entity. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for this field.

fields.name: serialised_event_data

Unlike many other NBT structures, this data is not actually in a compound but just loosely floating NBT tags. To decode using the nbt package, you would need to append 0x0a00 at the start (compound id and name length) and add 0x00 at the end, to manually wrap it in a compound. packets.name: StructureTemplateDataRequest
packets.title: 结构模板数据请求
packets.usage: 请求结构区域或模板数据；建筑导出相关，不是第三方网页转换。
packets.description: StructureTemplateDataRequest is sent by the client to request data of a structure.
packets.content:
## 132 · StructureTemplateDataRequest · 结构模板数据请求

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：客户端→服务器
- 用法与边界：请求结构区域或模板数据；建筑导出相关，不是第三方网页转换。
- 本内核原始说明：StructureTemplateDataRequest is sent by the client to request data of a structure.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `structure_name` | `string` | StructureName is the name of the structure that was set in the structure block's UI. This is the name used to export the structure to a file. |
| `position` | `protocol.BlockPos` | 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is the position of the structure block that has its template data requested. |
| `settings` | `protocol.StructureSettings` | Settings is a struct of settings that should be used for exporting the structure. These settings are identical to the last sent in the StructureBlockUpdate packet by the client. |
| `request_type` | `uint8` | RequestType specifies the type of template data request that the player sent. It is one of the constants found above. |

### settings 嵌套字段

- `palette_name` (`string`)：PaletteName is the name of the palette used in the structure. Currently, it seems that this field is always 'default'.
- `ignore_entities` (`bool`)：IgnoreEntities specifies if the structure should ignore entities or include them. If set to false, entities will also show up in the exported structure.
- `ignore_blocks` (`bool`)：IgnoreBlocks specifies if the structure should ignore blocks or include them. If set to false, blocks will show up in the exported structure.
- `allow_non_ticking_chunks` (`bool`)：AllowNonTickingChunks specifies if the structure should allow non-ticking chunks. If set to false, the structure will export non-ticking chunks.
- `size` (`BlockPos`)：Size is the size of the area that is about to be exported. The area exported will start at the Position + Offset, and will extend as far as Size specifies.
- `offset` (`BlockPos`)：Offset is the offset position that was set in the structure block. The area exported is offset by this position.
- `last_editing_player_unique_id` (`int64`)：LastEditingPlayerUniqueID is the unique ID of the player that last edited the structure block that these settings concern.
- `rotation` (`byte`)：Rotation is the rotation that the structure block should obtain. See the constants above for available options.
- `mirror` (`byte`)：Mirror specifies the way the structure should be mirrored. It is either no mirror at all, mirror on the x/z axis or both.
- `animation_mode` (`byte`)：AnimationMode ...
- `animation_duration` (`float32`)：AnimationDuration ...
- `integrity` (`float32`)：Integrity is usually 1, but may be set to a number between 0 and 1 to omit blocks randomly, using the Seed that follows.
- `seed` (`uint32`)：Seed is the seed used to omit blocks if Integrity is not equal to one. If the Seed is 0, a random seed is selected to omit blocks.
- `pivot` (`mgl32.Vec3`)：Pivot is the pivot around which the structure may be rotated.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|

fields.name: blobs
fields.note: Blobs is a list of all blobs that the client sent misses for in the ClientCacheBlobStatus. These blobs hold the data of the blobs with the hashes they are matched with.

children.name: hash
children.note: Hash is the hash of the blob. The hash is computed using xxHash, and must be deterministic for the same chunk data.

children.name: payload
children.note: Payload is the data of the blob. When sent, the client will associate the Hash of the blob with the Payload in it.

packets.content:
## 136 · ClientCacheMissResponse · 缓存缺失数据响应

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `blobs` | `[]protocol.CacheBlob` | Blobs is a list of all blobs that the client sent misses for in the ClientCacheBlobStatus. These blobs hold the data of the blobs with the hashes they are matched with. |

### blobs 嵌套字段

- `hash` (`uint64`)：Hash is the hash of the blob. The hash is computed using xxHash, and must be deterministic for the same chunk data.
- `payload` (`[]byte`)：Payload is the data of the blob. When sent, the client will associate the Hash of the blob with the Payload in it.

children.name: legacy_request_id
children.note: LegacyRequestID is an ID that is only non-zero at times when sent by the client. The server should always send 0 for this. When this field is not 0, the LegacySetItemSlots slice below will have values in it. LegacyRequestID ties in with the ItemStackResponse packet. If this field is non-0, the server should respond with an ItemStackResponse packet. Some inventory actions such as dropping an item out of the hotbar are still one using this packet, and the ItemStackResponse packet needs to tie in with it.

children.name: legacy_set_item_slots
children.note: LegacySetItemSlots are only present if the LegacyRequestID is non-zero. These item slots inform the server of the slots that were changed during the inventory transaction, and the server should send back an ItemStackResponse packet with these slots present in it. (Or false with no slots, if rejected.)

children.name: actions
children.note: Actions is a list of actions that took place, that form the inventory transaction together. Each of these actions hold one slot in which one item was changed to another. In general, the combination of all of these actions results in a balanced inventory transaction. This should be checked to ensure that no items are cheated into the inventory.

children.name: old_item
children.note: OldItem is the item that was present in the slot before the inventory action. It should be checked by the server to ensure the inventories were not out of sync.

- `actions.new_item.stack.can_be_placed_on` (`[]string`)：CanBePlacedOn is a list of block identifiers like 'minecraft:stone' which the item, if it is an item that can be placed, can be placed on top of.
- `actions.new_item.stack.can_break` (`[]string`)：CanBreak is a list of block identifiers like 'minecraft:dirt' that the item is able to break.
- `actions.new_item.stack.has_network_id` (`bool`)：HasNetworkID ...
- `action_type` (`uint32`)：ActionType is the type of the UseItem inventory transaction. It is one of the action types found above, and specifies the way the player interacted with the block.
- `trigger_type` (`uint32`)：TriggerType is the type of the trigger that caused the inventory transaction. It is one of the trigger types found in the constants above. If TriggerType is TriggerTypePlayerInput, the transaction is from the initial input of the player. If it is TriggerTypeSimulationTick, the transaction is from a simulation tick when the player is holding down the input.
- `block_position` (`BlockPos`)：BlockPosition is the position of the block that was interacted with. This is only really a correct block position if ActionType is not UseItemActionClickAir.
- `block_face` (`int32`)：BlockFace is the face of the block that was interacted with. When clicking the block, it is the face clicked. When breaking the block, it is the face that was last being hit until the block broke.
- `hot_bar_slot` (`int32`)：HotBarSlot is the hot bar slot that the player was holding while clicking the block. It should be used to ensure that the hot bar slot and held item are correctly synchronised with the server.
- `held_item` (`ItemInstance`)：HeldItem is the item that was held to interact with the block. The server should check if this item is actually present in the HotBarSlot.
- `held_item.stack_network_id` (`int32`)：StackNetworkID is the network ID of the item stack. If the stack is empty, 0 is always written for this field. If not, the field should be set to 1 if the server authoritative inventories are disabled in the StartGame packet, or to a unique stack ID if it is enabled.
- `held_item.stack` (`ItemStack`)：Stack is the actual item stack of the item instance.
- `held_item.stack.block_runtime_id` (`int32`)：BlockRuntimeID ...
- `held_item.stack.count` (`uint16`)：Count is the count of items that the item stack holds.
- `held_item.stack.nbtdata` (`map[string]any`)：NBTData is a map that is serialised to its NBT representation when sent in a packet.
- `held_item.stack.can_be_placed_on` (`[]string`)：CanBePlacedOn is a list of block identifiers like 'minecraft:stone' which the item, if it is an item that can be placed, can be placed on top of.
- `held_item.stack.can_break` (`[]string`)：CanBreak is a list of block identifiers like 'minecraft:dirt' that the item is able to break.
- `held_item.stack.has_network_id` (`bool`)：HasNetworkID ...
- `position` (`mgl32.Vec3`)：Position is the position of the player at the time of interaction. For clicking a block, this is the position at that time, whereas for breaking the block it is the position at the time of breaking.
- `clicked_position` (`mgl32.Vec3`)：ClickedPosition is the position that was clicked relative to the block's base coordinate. It can be used to find out exactly where a player clicked the block.
- `block_runtime_id` (`uint32`)：BlockRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the block that was clicked. It may be used by the server to verify that the player's world client-side is synchronised with the server's.
- `client_prediction` (`uint32`)：ClientPrediction is the client's prediction on the output of the transaction. It is one of the client prediction found in the constants above.

### item_stack_request 嵌套字段

- `request_id` (`int32`)：RequestID is a unique ID for the request. This ID is used by the server to send a response for this specific request in the ItemStackResponse packet.
- `actions` (`[]StackRequestAction`)：Actions is a list of actions performed by the client. The actual type of the actions depends on which ID was present, and is one of the concrete types below.
- `filter_strings` (`[]string`)：FilterStrings is a list of filter strings involved in the request. This is typically filled with one string when an anvil or cartography is used.
- `filter_cause` (`int32`)：FilterCause represents the cause of any potential filtering. This is one of the constants above.

### block_actions 嵌套字段

- `action` (`int32`)：Action is the action to be performed, and is one of the constants listed above.
- `block_pos` (`BlockPos`)：BlockPos is the position of the block that was interacted with.
- `face` (`int32`)：Face is the face of the block that was interacted with.

packets.name: CreativeContent
packets.title: 创造物品目录
packets.usage: 服务端下发可用创造物品；列在目录不代表当前账号可取用。
packets.description: CreativeContent is a packet sent by the server to set the creative inventory's content for a player. Introduced in 1.16, this packet replaces the previous method - sending an InventoryContent packet with creative inventory window ID. As of v1.21.60, this packet is no longer required to be sent as part of the login sequence however the client will crash if they try to open their creative inventory before receiving this packet. Every item must be part of a group, any items that are not part of a group will need to reference an "anonymous group" which has an empty name OR no icon. The order of Groups and Items is how the client will render items in the creative inventory compared to the previous, hard coded order.  Below is an example of defining 2 ungrouped items, 2 grouped items and then another 2 ungrouped items, all in the nature category.  CreativeContent{ Groups: []protocol.CreativeGroup{ {Category: 1}, // No name or icon, this is the "anonymous group" {Category: 1, Name: "itemGroup.name.planks", Icon: protocol.ItemStack{...}}, // A "planks" group {Category: 1}, // Another "anonymous group" }, Items: []protocol.CreativeItem{ {CreativeItemNetworkID: 0, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 0}, // Ungrouped before "planks" {CreativeItemNetworkID: 1, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 0}, // Ungrouped before "planks" {CreativeItemNetworkID: 2, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 1}, // Grouped under the "planks" group {CreativeItemNetworkID: 3, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 1}, // Grouped under the "planks" group {CreativeItemNetworkID: 4, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 2}, // Ungrouped after "planks" {CreativeItemNetworkID: 5, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 2}, // Ungrouped after "planks" } }

fields.name: options
fields.note: Options is a list of possible enchantment options for the item that was put into the enchantment table.

children.name: cost
children.note: Cost is the cost of the option. This is the amount of XP levels required to select this enchantment option.

children.name: enchantments
children.note: Enchantments holds the enchantments that will be applied to the item when this option is clicked.

children.name: slot
children.note: Slot is either 0, 1 or 2. Its exact usage is not clear.

children.name: enchantments
children.note: Enchantments is an array of 3 slices of enchantment instances. Each array represents enchantments that will be added to the item with a different activation type. The arrays in which enchantments are sent by the vanilla server are as follows: slice 1 { protection, fire protection, feather falling, blast protection, projectile protection, thorns, respiration, depth strider, aqua affinity, frost walker, soul speed } slice 2 { sharpness, smite, bane of arthropods, fire aspect, looting, silk touch, unbreaking, fortune, flame, luck of the sea, impaling } slice 3 { knockback, efficiency, power, punch, infinity, lure, mending, curse of binding, curse of vanishing, riptide, loyalty, channeling, multishot, piercing, quick charge } The first slice holds armour enchantments, the differences between the slice 2 and slice 3 are more vaguely defined.

children.name: name
children.note: Name is a name that will be translated to the 'Standard Galactic Alphabet' (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Enchanting_Table#Standard_Galactic_Alphabet) client-side. The names generally have no meaning, such as: 'animal imbue range galvanize ' 'bless inside creature shrink ' 'elder free of inside '

children.name: recipe_network_id
children.note: RecipeNetworkID is a unique network ID for this enchantment option. When enchanting, the client will submit this network ID in a ItemStackRequest packet with the CraftRecipe action, so that the server knows which enchantment was selected. Note that this ID should still be unique with other actual recipes. It's recommended to start counting for enchantment network IDs from the counter used for producing network IDs for the normal recipes.

packets.name: PlayerEnchantOptions
packets.title: 玩家附魔选项
packets.usage: 用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
packets.description: PlayerEnchantOptions is sent by the server to update the enchantment options displayed when the user opens the enchantment table and puts an item in. This packet was added in 1.16 and allows the server to decide on the enchantments that can be selected by the player. The PlayerEnchantOptions packet should be sent once for every slot update of the enchantment table. The vanilla server sends an empty PlayerEnchantOptions packet when the player opens the enchantment table (air is present in the enchantment table slot) and sends the packet with actual enchantments in it when items are put in that can have enchantments.

packets.name: ItemStackRequest

packets.usage: 移动、交换、丢弃、合成等操作，由服务器校验，不能伪造得到任意物品。
packets.description: ItemStackRequest represents a single request present in an ItemStackRequest packet sent by the client to change an item in an inventory. Item stack requests are either approved or rejected by the server using the ItemStackResponse packet.
packets.content:
## 147 · ItemStackRequest · 现代物品栈请求

- 分组：物品与容器
- 方向：客户端→服务器
- 用法与边界：移动、交换、丢弃、合成等操作，由服务器校验，不能伪造得到任意物品。
- 本内核原始说明：ItemStackRequest represents a single request present in an ItemStackRequest packet sent by the client to change an item in an inventory. Item stack requests are either approved or rejected by the server using the ItemStackResponse packet.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `requests` | `[]protocol.ItemStackRequest` |  |

### requests 嵌套字段

- `request_id` (`int32`)：RequestID is a unique ID for the request. This ID is used by the server to send a response for this specific request in the ItemStackResponse packet.
- `actions` (`[]StackRequestAction`)：Actions is a list of actions performed by the client. The actual type of the actions depends on which ID was present, and is one of the concrete types below.
- `filter_strings` (`[]string`)：FilterStrings is a list of filter strings involved in the request. This is typically filled with one string when an anvil or cartography is used.
- `filter_cause` (`int32`)：FilterCause represents the cause of any potential filtering. This is one of the constants above.

children.name: status
children.note: Status specifies if the request with the RequestID below was successful. If this is the case, the ContainerInfo below will have information on what slots ended up changing. If not, the container info will be empty. A non-0 status means an error occurred and will result in the action being reverted.

children.name: request_id
children.note: RequestID is the unique ID of the request that this response is in reaction to. If rejected, the client will undo the actions from the request with this ID.

children.name: container_info
children.note: ContainerInfo holds information on the containers that had their contents changed as a result of the request.

children.name: container
children.note: Container is the FullContainerName that describes the container that the slots that follow are in. For the main inventory, the ContainerID seems to be 0x1b. Fur the cursor, this value seems to be 0x3a. For the crafting grid, this value seems to be 0x0d.

children.name: container_id
children.note: ContainerID is the ID of the container that the slot was in.

children.name: dynamic_container_id
children.note: DynamicContainerID is the ID of the container if it is dynamic. If the container is not dynamic, this field should be left empty. A non-optional value of 0 is assumed to be non-empty.

children.name: slot_info
children.note: SlotInfo holds information on what item stack should be present in specific slots in the container.

children.name: count
children.note: Count is the total count of the item stack. This count will be shown client-side after the response is sent to the client.

children.name: stack_network_id
children.note: StackNetworkID is the network ID of the new stack at a specific slot.

children.name: custom_name
children.note: CustomName is the custom name of the item stack. It is used in relation to text filtering.

children.name: filtered_custom_name
children.note: FilteredCustomName is a filtered version of CustomName with all the profanity removed. The client will use this over CustomName if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

children.name: durability_correction
children.note: DurabilityCorrection is the current durability of the item stack. This durability will be shown client-side after the response is sent to the client.

packets.usage: 匹配请求ID看成功失败与槽位，不将请求发送当事务成功。
packets.description: ItemStackResponse is a response to an individual ItemStackRequest.
packets.content:
## 148 · ItemStackResponse · 物品栈请求响应

- 分组：物品与容器
- 方向：服务器→本机客户端
- 用法与边界：匹配请求ID看成功失败与槽位，不将请求发送当事务成功。
- 本内核原始说明：ItemStackResponse is a response to an individual ItemStackRequest.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `responses` | `[]protocol.ItemStackResponse` |  |

### responses 嵌套字段

- `status` (`uint8`)：Status specifies if the request with the RequestID below was successful. If this is the case, the ContainerInfo below will have information on what slots ended up changing. If not, the container info will be empty. A non-0 status means an error occurred and will result in the action being reverted.
- `request_id` (`int32`)：RequestID is the unique ID of the request that this response is in reaction to. If rejected, the client will undo the actions from the request with this ID.
- `container_info` (`[]StackResponseContainerInfo`)：ContainerInfo holds information on the containers that had their contents changed as a result of the request.
- `container_info.container` (`FullContainerName`)：Container is the FullContainerName that describes the container that the slots that follow are in. For the main inventory, the ContainerID seems to be 0x1b. Fur the cursor, this value seems to be 0x3a. For the crafting grid, this value seems to be 0x0d.
- `container_info.container.container_id` (`byte`)：ContainerID is the ID of the container that the slot was in.
- `container_info.container.dynamic_container_id` (`Optional[uint32]`)：DynamicContainerID is the ID of the container if it is dynamic. If the container is not dynamic, this field should be left empty. A non-optional value of 0 is assumed to be non-empty.
- `container_info.slot_info` (`[]StackResponseSlotInfo`)：SlotInfo holds information on what item stack should be present in specific slots in the container.
- `container_info.slot_info.count` (`byte`)：Count is the total count of the item stack. This count will be shown client-side after the response is sent to the client.
- `container_info.slot_info.stack_network_id` (`int32`)：StackNetworkID is the network ID of the new stack at a specific slot.
- `container_info.slot_info.custom_name` (`string`)：CustomName is the custom name of the item stack. It is used in relation to text filtering.
- `container_info.slot_info.filtered_custom_name` (`string`)：FilteredCustomName is a filtered version of CustomName with all the profanity removed. The client will use this over CustomName if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.
- `container_info.slot_info.durability_correction` (`int32`)：DurabilityCorrection is the current durability of the item stack. This durability will be shown client-side after the response is sent to the client.

fields.name: bitset

packets.content:
## 149 · PlayerArmourDamage · 玩家护甲伤害

fields.name: broadcast_action
fields.note: BroadcastAction specifies the status of the position tracking DB response. It is one of the constants above, specifying the result of the request with the ID below. The Update action is sent for setting the position of a lodestone compass, the Destroy and NotFound to indicate that there is not (no longer) a lodestone at that position.

fields.name: tracking_id
fields.note: TrackingID is the ID of the PositionTrackingDBClientRequest packet that this packet was in response to. The tracking ID is also present as the 'id' field in the SerialisedData field.

fields.name: payload
fields.note: Payload is a network little endian compound tag holding the data retrieved from the position tracking DB. An example data structure sent if BroadcastAction is of the type Update: TAG_Compound({ 'version': TAG_Byte(0x01), 'dim': TAG_Int(0), 'id': TAG_String(0x00000001), 'pos': TAG_List<TAG_Int>({ -299, 86, 74, }), 'status': TAG_Byte(0x00), // 0x00 for updating, 0x02 for not found/block destroyed. })

packets.name: PositionTrackingDBServerBroadcast
packets.title: 位置追踪数据库广播
packets.usage: 位置追踪标识和数据；不是查询全部玩家坐标的万能入口。
packets.description: PositionTrackingDBServerBroadcast is sent by the server in response to the PositionTrackingDBClientRequest packet. This packet is, as of 1.16, currently only used for lodestones. The server maintains a database with tracking IDs and their position and dimension. The client will request these tracking IDs, (NBT tag set on the lodestone compass with the tracking ID?) and the server will respond with the status of those tracking IDs. What is actually done with the data sent depends on what the client chooses to do with it. For the lodestone compass, it is used to make the compass point towards lodestones and to make it spin if the lodestone at a position is no longer there.

The server maintains a database with tracking IDs and their position and dimension. The client will request these tracking IDs, (NBT tag set on the lodestone compass with the tracking ID?) and the server will respond with the status of those tracking IDs. What is actually done with the data sent depends on what the client chooses to do with it. For the lodestone compass, it is used to make the compass point towards lodestones and to make it spin if the lodestone at a position is no longer there.

An example data structure sent if BroadcastAction is of the type Update: TAG_Compound({ 'version': TAG_Byte(0x01), 'dim': TAG_Int(0), 'id': TAG_String(0x00000001), 'pos': TAG_List<TAG_Int>({ -299, 86, 74, }), 'status': TAG_Byte(0x00), // 0x00 for updating, 0x02 for not found/block destroyed. }) |

In 1.16, this is used for lodestones. The client will send this request to find the position a lodestone compass needs to point to. If found, it will point to the lodestone. packets.usage: 对应SubChunkRequest，需按当前维度与调色板解析；不能把原始payload_hex当方块名。
packets.description: SubChunk sends data about multiple sub-chunks around a center point.
packets.content:
## 174 · SubChunk · 子区块响应

- 分组：世界与结构
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：对应SubChunkRequest，需按当前维度与调色板解析；不能把原始payload_hex当方块名。
- 本内核原始说明：SubChunk sends data about multiple sub-chunks around a center point.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `cache_enabled` | `bool` | CacheEnabled is whether the sub-chunk caching is enabled or not. |
| `dimension` | `int32` | Dimension is the dimension the sub-chunks are in. |
| `position` | `protocol.SubChunkPos` | 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is an absolute sub-chunk center point that every SubChunkRequest uses as a reference. |
| `sub_chunk_entries` | `[]protocol.SubChunkEntry` | SubChunkEntries contains sub-chunk entries relative to the center point. |
| `block_entities` | `[]uint8` | BlockEntities contains the trailing NBT block entity data after all sub-chunk entries. This data is only present when the server sends block entities in the SubChunk response. |

### sub_chunk_entries 嵌套字段

- `offset` (`SubChunkOffset`)：Offset contains the offset between the sub-chunk position and the center position.
- `result` (`byte`)：Result is always one of the constants defined in the SubChunkResult constants.
- `raw_payload` (`[]byte`)：RawPayload contains the serialized sub-chunk data.
- `height_map_type` (`byte`)：HeightMapType is always one of the constants defined in the HeightMapData constants.
- `height_map_data` (`[]int8`)：HeightMapData is the data for the height map.
- `render_height_map_type` (`byte`)：RenderHeightMapType is always one of the constants defined in the HeightMapData constants.
- `render_height_map_data` (`[]int8`)：RenderHeightMapData is the data for the render height map.
- `blob_hash` (`uint64`)：BlobHash is the hash of the blob.

fields.name: dimension
fields.note: Dimension is the dimension of the sub-chunk.

fields.name: position
fields.note: 位置坐标，维度与有效性按本包上下文确定。 Position is an absolute sub-chunk center point used as a base point for all sub-chunks requested. The X and Z coordinates represent the chunk coordinates, while the Y coordinate is the absolute sub-chunk index.

packets.title: 实体能力与权限同步
packets.usage: 真实能力位和权限等级，可查当前授予能力，不等于可以自行授予。
packets.description: UpdateAbilities is a packet sent from the server to the client to update the abilities of the player. It, along with the UpdateAdventureSettings packet, are replacements of the AdventureSettings packet since v1.19.10.
packets.content:
## 187 · UpdateAbilities · 实体能力与权限同步

- 分组：权限与会话
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：真实能力位和权限等级，可查当前授予能力，不等于可以自行授予。
- 本内核原始说明：UpdateAbilities is a packet sent from the server to the client to update the abilities of the player. It, along with the UpdateAdventureSettings packet, are replacements of the AdventureSettings packet since v1.19.10.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `ability_data` | `protocol.AbilityData` | AbilityData represents various data about the abilities of a player, such as ability layers or permissions. |

### ability_data 嵌套字段

- `entity_unique_id` (`int64`)：EntityUniqueID is a unique identifier of the player. It appears it is not required to fill this field out with a correct value. Simply writing 0 seems to work.
- `player_permissions` (`byte`)：PlayerPermissions is the permission level of the player as it shows up in the player list built up using the PlayerList packet.
- `command_permissions` (`byte`)：CommandPermissions is a set of permissions that specify what commands a player is allowed to execute.
- `layers` (`[]AbilityLayer`)：Layers contains all ability layers and their potential values. This should at least have one entry, being the base layer.
- `layers.type` (`uint16`)：Type represents the type of the layer. This is one of the AbilityLayerType constants defined above.
- `layers.abilities` (`uint32`)：Abilities is a set of abilities that are enabled for the layer. This is one of the Ability constants defined above.
- `layers.values` (`uint32`)：Values is a set of values that are associated with the enabled abilities, representing the values of the abilities.
- `layers.fly_speed` (`float32`)：FlySpeed is the default horizontal fly speed of the layer.
- `layers.vertical_fly_speed` (`float32`)：VerticalFlySpeed is the default vertical fly speed of the layer.
- `layers.walk_speed` (`float32`)：WalkSpeed is the default walk speed of the layer.

- `layers` (`[]AbilityLayer`)：Layers contains all ability layers and their potential values. This should at least have one entry, being the base layer.

fields.name: presets
fields.note: Presets is a list of camera presets that can be used by other cameras. The order of this list is important because the index of presets is used as a pointer in the CameraInstruction packet.

children.name: name
children.note: Name is the name of the preset. Each preset must have their own unique name.

children.name: parent
children.note: Parent is the name of the preset that this preset extends upon. This can be left empty.

children.name: pos_x
children.note: PosX is the default X position of the camera.

children.name: pos_y
children.note: PosY is the default Y position of the camera.

children.name: pos_z
children.note: PosZ is the default Z position of the camera.

children.name: rot_x
children.note: RotX is the default pitch of the camera.

children.name: rot_y
children.note: RotY is the default yaw of the camera.

children.name: rotation_speed
children.note: RotationSpeed is the speed at which the camera should rotate.

children.name: snap_to_target
children.note: SnapToTarget determines whether the camera should snap to the target entity or not.

children.name: horizontal_rotation_limit
children.note: HorizontalRotationLimit is the horizontal rotation limit of the camera.

children.name: vertical_rotation_limit
children.note: VerticalRotationLimit is the vertical rotation limit of the camera.

children.name: continue_targeting
children.note: ContinueTargeting determines whether the camera should continue targeting when using aim assist.

children.name: tracking_radius
children.note: TrackingRadius is the radius around the camera that the aim assist should track targets.

children.name: view_offset
children.note: ViewOffset is only used in a follow_orbit camera and controls an offset based on a pivot point to the player, causing it to be shifted in a certain direction.

children.name: entity_offset
children.note: EntityOffset controls the offset from the entity that the camera should be rendered at.

children.name: radius
children.note: Radius is only used in a follow_orbit camera and controls how far away from the player the camera should be rendered.

children.name: min_yaw_limit
children.note: MinYawLimit is the minimum yaw limit of the camera.

children.name: max_yaw_limit
children.note: MaxYawLimit is the maximum yaw limit of the camera.

children.name: audio_listener
children.note: AudioListener defines where the audio should be played from when using this preset. This is one of the constants above.

children.name: player_effects
children.note: PlayerEffects is currently unknown.

children.name: aim_assist
children.note: AimAssist defines the aim assist to use when using this preset.

children.name: control_scheme
children.note: ControlScheme is the control scheme that the client should use in this camera. It is one of the following: - ControlSchemeLockedPlayerRelativeStrafe is the default behaviour, this cannot be set when the client is in a custom camera. - ControlSchemeCameraRelative makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the client's rotation being relative to the client's movement. - ControlSchemeCameraRelativeStrafe makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the client's rotation being locked. - ControlSchemePlayerRelative makes movement relative to the player's transform, meaning holding left/right will make the player turn in a circle. - ControlSchemePlayerRelativeStrafe makes movement the same as the default behaviour, but can be used in a custom camera.

It is one of the following: - ControlSchemeLockedPlayerRelativeStrafe is the default behaviour, this cannot be set when the client is in a custom camera. - ControlSchemeCameraRelative makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the client's rotation being relative to the client's movement. - ControlSchemeCameraRelativeStrafe makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the client's rotation being locked. - ControlSchemePlayerRelative makes movement relative to the player's transform, meaning holding left/right will make the player turn in a circle. - ControlSchemePlayerRelativeStrafe makes movement the same as the default behaviour, but can be used in a custom camera.

children.name: skin_resource_patch
children.note: SkinResourcePatch is a JSON encoded object holding some fields that point to the geometry that the skin has. The JSON object that this holds specifies the way that the geometry of animations and the default skin of the player are combined.

The ImageData contains FrameCount images in it, which each represent one stage of the animation. The actual part of the skin that this field holds depends on the AnimationType, where SkinAnimationHead holds only the head and its hat, whereas the other animations hold the entire body of the skin.

children.note: FrameCount is the amount of frames that the skin animation holds. The number of frames here is the amount of images that may be found in the ImageData field.

children.note: ExpressionType is the type of expression made by the skin, which is one the types found above.

children.note: CapeData is a byte slice of 64*32*4 bytes. It is a RGBA ordered byte representation of the cape colours, much like the SkinData.

children.note: ArmSize is the size of the arms of the player's model. This is either 'wide' (generally for male skins) or 'slim' (generally for female skins).

children.name: persona_pieces
children.note: PersonaPieces is a list of all persona pieces that the skin is composed of.

children.name: piece_id
children.note: PieceId is a UUID that identifies the piece itself, which is unique for each separate piece.

children.name: piece_type
children.note: PieceType holds the type of the piece. Several types I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_skeleton - persona_body - persona_skin - persona_bottom - persona_feet - persona_top - persona_mouth - persona_hair - persona_eyes - persona_facial_hair

children.name: pack_id
children.note: PackID is a UUID that identifies the pack that the persona piece belongs to.

children.name: default
children.note: Default specifies if the piece is one of the default pieces. This is true when the piece is one of those that a Steve or Alex skin have.

children.name: product_id
children.note: ProductID is a UUID that identifies the piece when it comes to purchases. It is empty for pieces that have the 'Default' field set to true.

children.name: piece_tint_colours
children.note: PieceTintColours is a list of specific tint colours for (some of) the persona pieces found in the list above.

children.name: piece_type
children.note: PieceType is the type of the persona skin piece that this tint colour concerns. The piece type must always be present in the persona pieces list, but not each piece type has a tint colour sent. Pieces that do have a tint colour that I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_mouth - persona_eyes - persona_hair

children.name: colours
children.note: Colours is a list four colours written in hex notation (note, that unlike the SkinColour field in the ClientData struct, this is actually ARGB, not just RGB). The colours refer to different parts of the skin piece. The 'persona_eyes' may have the following colours: ["#ffa12722","#ff2f1f0f","#ff3aafd9","#0"] The first hex colour represents the tint colour of the iris, the second hex colour represents the eyebrows and the third represents the sclera. The fourth is #0 because there are only 3 parts of the persona_eyes skin piece.

children.name: trusted
children.note: Trusted specifies if the skin is 'trusted'. No code should rely on this field, as any proxy or client can easily change it.

children.name: override_appearance
children.note: OverrideAppearance specifies if the skin should override the player's skin that is equipped client-side. When false, the client will reject the skin and continue to use the skin that the player has equipped.

### player_data 嵌套字段

- `unknown1` (`bool`)：Netease
- `uuid` (`uuid.UUID`)：Netease
- `unknown2` (`string`)：Netease

### skin 嵌套字段

- `skin_id` (`string`)：SkinID is a unique ID produced for the skin, for example 'c18e65aa-7b21-4637-9b63-8ad63622ef01_Alex' for the default Alex skin.
- `play_fab_id` (`string`)：PlayFabID is the PlayFab ID produced for the skin. PlayFab is the company that hosts the Marketplace, skins and other related features from the game. This ID is the ID of the skin used to store the skin inside of PlayFab.
- `skin_resource_patch` (`[]byte`)：SkinResourcePatch is a JSON encoded object holding some fields that point to the geometry that the skin has. The JSON object that this holds specifies the way that the geometry of animations and the default skin of the player are combined.
- `skin_data` (`[]byte`)：SkinData is a byte slice of SkinImageWidth * SkinImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte representation of the skin pixels.
- `animations` (`[]SkinAnimation`)：Animations is a list of all animations that the skin has.
- `animations.image_data` (`[]byte`)：ImageData is a byte slice of ImageWidth * ImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte representation of the animation image pixels. The ImageData contains FrameCount images in it, which each represent one stage of the animation. The actual part of the skin that this field holds depends on the AnimationType, where SkinAnimationHead holds only the head and its hat, whereas the other animations hold the entire body of the skin.
- `animations.animation_type` (`uint32`)：AnimationType is the type of the animation, which is one of the types found above. The data that ImageData contains depends on this type.
- `animations.frame_count` (`float32`)：FrameCount is the amount of frames that the skin animation holds. The number of frames here is the amount of images that may be found in the ImageData field.
- `animations.expression_type` (`uint32`)：ExpressionType is the type of expression made by the skin, which is one the types found above.
- `cape_data` (`[]byte`)：CapeData is a byte slice of 64*32*4 bytes. It is a RGBA ordered byte representation of the cape colours, much like the SkinData.
- `skin_geometry` (`[]byte`)：SkinGeometry is a JSON encoded structure of the geometry data of a skin, containing properties such as bones, uv, pivot etc.
- `animation_data` (`[]byte`)：TODO: Find out what value AnimationData holds and when it does hold something.
- `geometry_data_engine_version` (`[]byte`)：GeometryDataEngineVersion ...
- `premium_skin` (`bool`)：PremiumSkin specifies if this is a skin that was purchased from the marketplace.
- `persona_skin` (`bool`)：PersonaSkin specifies if this is a skin that was created using the in-game skin creator.
- `persona_cape_on_classic_skin` (`bool`)：PersonaCapeOnClassicSkin specifies if the skin had a Persona cape (in-game skin creator cape) equipped on a classic skin.
- `primary_user` (`bool`)：PrimaryUser ...
- `cape_id` (`string`)：CapeID is a unique identifier that identifies the cape. It usually holds a UUID in it.
- `full_id` (`string`)：FullID is an ID that represents the skin in full. The actual functionality is unknown: The client does not seem to send a value for this.
- `skin_colour` (`string`)：SkinColour is a hex representation (including #) of the base colour of the skin. An example of the colour sent here is '#b37b62'.
- `arm_size` (`string`)：ArmSize is the size of the arms of the player's model. This is either 'wide' (generally for male skins) or 'slim' (generally for female skins).
- `persona_pieces` (`[]PersonaPiece`)：PersonaPieces is a list of all persona pieces that the skin is composed of.
- `persona_pieces.piece_id` (`string`)：PieceId is a UUID that identifies the piece itself, which is unique for each separate piece.
- `persona_pieces.piece_type` (`string`)：PieceType holds the type of the piece. Several types I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_skeleton - persona_body - persona_skin - persona_bottom - persona_feet - persona_top - persona_mouth - persona_hair - persona_eyes - persona_facial_hair
- `persona_pieces.pack_id` (`string`)：PackID is a UUID that identifies the pack that the persona piece belongs to.
- `persona_pieces.default` (`bool`)：Default specifies if the piece is one of the default pieces. This is true when the piece is one of those that a Steve or Alex skin have.
- `persona_pieces.product_id` (`string`)：ProductID is a UUID that identifies the piece when it comes to purchases. It is empty for pieces that have the 'Default' field set to true.
- `piece_tint_colours` (`[]PersonaPieceTintColour`)：PieceTintColours is a list of specific tint colours for (some of) the persona pieces found in the list above.
- `piece_tint_colours.piece_type` (`string`)：PieceType is the type of the persona skin piece that this tint colour concerns. The piece type must always be present in the persona pieces list, but not each piece type has a tint colour sent. Pieces that do have a tint colour that I was able to find immediately are listed below. - persona_mouth - persona_eyes - persona_hair
- `piece_tint_colours.colours` (`[]string`)：Colours is a list four colours written in hex notation (note, that unlike the SkinColour field in the ClientData struct, this is actually ARGB, not just RGB). The colours refer to different parts of the skin piece. The 'persona_eyes' may have the following colours: ["#ffa12722","#ff2f1f0f","#ff3aafd9","#0"] The first hex colour represents the tint colour of the iris, the second hex colour represents the eyebrows and the third represents the sclera. The fourth is #0 because there are only 3 parts of the persona_eyes skin piece.
- `trusted` (`bool`)：Trusted specifies if the skin is 'trusted'. No code should rely on this field, as any proxy or client can easily change it.
- `override_appearance` (`bool`)：OverrideAppearance specifies if the skin should override the player's skin that is equipped client-side. When false, the client will reject the skin and continue to use the skin that the player has equipped.

packets.description: CameraAimAssistPresets is sent by the server to the client to provide a list of categories and presets that can be used when sending a CameraAimAssist packet or a CameraInstruction including aim assist.
packets.content:
## 320 · CameraAimAssistPresets · 摄像机瞄准辅助预设

- 分组：其他协议功能
- 方向：服务器→客户端
- 用法与边界：用途按本内核原始定义说明；不自动赋予额外游戏权限。
- 本内核原始说明：CameraAimAssistPresets is sent by the server to the client to provide a list of categories and presets that can be used when sending a CameraAimAssist packet or a CameraInstruction including aim assist.

| 字段 | 当前类型 | 语义与约束 |
|---|---|---|
| `categories` | `[]protocol.CameraAimAssistCategory` | Categories is a list of categories which can be referenced by one of the Presets. |
| `presets` | `[]protocol.CameraAimAssistPreset` | Presets is a list of presets which define a base for how aim assist should behave |
| `operation` | `uint8` | Operation is the operation to perform with the presets. It is one of the constants above. |

### categories 嵌套字段

- `name` (`string`)：Name is the name of the category which can be used by a CameraAimAssistPreset.
- `priorities` (`CameraAimAssistPriorities`)：Priorities represents the block and entity specific priorities as well as the default priorities for this category.
- `priorities.entities` (`[]CameraAimAssistPriority`)：Entities is a list of priorities for specific entity identifiers.
- `priorities.entities.identifier` (`string`)：Identifier is the identifier of a target to define the priority for.
- `priorities.entities.priority` (`int32`)：Priority is the priority for this specific target.
- `priorities.blocks` (`[]CameraAimAssistPriority`)：Blocks is a list of priorities for specific block identifiers.
- `priorities.blocks.identifier` (`string`)：Identifier is the identifier of a target to define the priority for.
- `priorities.blocks.priority` (`int32`)：Priority is the priority for this specific target.
- `priorities.entity_default` (`Optional[int32]`)：EntityDefault is the default priority for entities.
- `priorities.block_default` (`Optional[int32]`)：BlockDefault is the default priority for blocks.

### presets 嵌套字段

- `identifier` (`string`)：Identifier represents the identifier of this preset.
- `block_exclusions` (`[]string`)：BlockExclusions is a list of block identifiers that should be ignored by the aim assist.
- `liquid_targets` (`[]string`)：LiquidTargets is a list of entity identifiers that should be targetted when inside of a liquid.
- `item_settings` (`[]CameraAimAssistItemSettings`)：ItemSettings is a list of settings for specific item identifiers. If an item is not listed here, it will fallback to DefaultItemSettings or HandSettings if no item is held.
- `item_settings.item` (`string`)：Item is the identifier of the item to apply the settings to.
- `item_settings.category` (`string`)：Category is the identifier of a category to use which has been defined by a CameraAimAssistCategory. Only categories defined in the Categories slice used by the CameraAimAssistPreset can be used here.
- `default_item_settings` (`Optional[string]`)：DefaultItemSettings is the identifier of a category to use when the player is not holding an item listed in ItemSettings. This must be the identifier of a category within the Categories slice.
- `hand_settings` (`Optional[string]`)：HandSettings is the identifier of a category to use when the player is not holding an item. This must be the identifier of a category within Categories slice.

fields.note: Action is the action to perform with the aim assist. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: control_scheme
fields.note: ControlScheme is the control scheme that the client should use. It is one of the following: - ControlSchemeLockedPlayerRelativeStrafe is the default behaviour, this cannot be set when the client is in a custom camera. - ControlSchemeCameraRelative makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the client's rotation being relative to the client's movement. - ControlSchemeCameraRelativeStrafe makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the client's rotation being locked. - ControlSchemePlayerRelative makes movement relative to the player's transform, meaning holding left/right will make the player turn in a circle. - ControlSchemePlayerRelativeStrafe makes movement the same as the default behaviour, but can be used in a custom camera.
